body.input: The following is a conversation with Douglas Murray, author of The Madness of Crowds, Gender,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Race and Identity, and his most recent book, The War in the West, How to Prevail in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Age of Unreason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: He's a brilliant, fearless, and often controversial thinker who points out and pushes back against

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: what he sees as the madness of our modern world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I should note that the use of the word Marxism and the West in this conversation refers primarily

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: to cultural Marxism and the cultural values of Western civilization, respectively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: This is in contrast to my previous conversation with Richard Wolff where we focused on Marxism

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: as primarily a critique of capitalism and thus looking at it through the lens of economics

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: and not culture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Nevertheless, these two episodes stand opposite of each other with very different perspectives

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: on how we build a flourishing civilization together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I leave it to you, the listener, to think and to decide which is the better way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman Podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And now, dear friends, here's Douglas Murray.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: You recently wrote the book titled The War on the West, which in part says that the values,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: ideas, and history of Western civilization are under attack.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: So let's start with the basics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Historically and today, what are the ideas that represent Western civilization?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: The good, the bad, the ugly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I actually don't get stuck on definitions precisely because as you know, once you get

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: stuck on definitions, there's a possibility you'll never get off them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I'd say a few things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Firstly, obviously the Western tradition is a specific tradition, a specific tradition

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: of ideas, culture, well known to be perhaps easily defined by the combination of Athens

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: and Jerusalem, the world of the Bible, and the world of ancient Greece and indeed Rome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Effectively creates European civilization, which itself spawns the rest of the Western

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: civilizations, America, Canada, Australia, New Zealand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: But these are the main countries that we still refer to as the West.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: So there's a specific tradition and all the things that come from it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: My shorthand cheat on this answer is to say, you know when you're not in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: So if you've ever been to Beijing, Shanghai, you know you're not in the West, somewhere

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: You know you're not in the West.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: When you're in Tokyo, somewhere extraordinary, but you know you're not in the West.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Obviously there are, let's say borderline questions like is Russia in the West?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Which I sort of leave open as a question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Possibly if you were placed into Moscow blindfolded and you woke up and you couldn't hear the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: language or maybe you didn't know what the language sounded like, would you, would you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: guess you were in the West or not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I think I was somewhere near it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Getting closer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I mean, you know, it's also asked the question, doesn't it, whether it's European.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And I think the answer to that is not really, although massively influenced by Europe, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: and times wanting to reach towards it at times wanting to stay away, but a part of the West,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: possibly, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: But anyway, it's a very specific tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: It's one of a number of major traditions in the world and because it's hard to define

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: doesn't mean it doesn't exist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Are there certain characteristics and qualities about the values and the ideas that define

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: it is, is the type of rule, the type of governmental structure?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I mean the rule of law, property owning democracies and much more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I mean, these are of course things that were ended up being developed in America and then

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: given back to much of the rest of the West.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I say there are other perhaps more controversial attributes I would give to the West.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: One is a ravenous interest in the rest of the world, which is not shared of course by

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: every other culture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: The late philosopher George Steiner said he could never get out of his head the haunting

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: fact that the boats only seemed to go out from Europe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: They didn't, the explorers, the scholars, the linguists, the people who wanted to discover

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: other civilizations and indeed even resurrect ancient civilizations and lost civilizations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: These were scholars that were always coming from the West to discover this elsewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: By contrast, there were never boats coming from Egypt to help the Anglo-Saxons discover

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: the origins of their language and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: So I think there is a sort of ravenous interest in the rest of the world, which can be said

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: to be a Western attribute, although it of course also has, one should immediately preface

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: it, some downsides and many criticisms that can be made of some of the consequences of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: that interest because of course it's not entirely lacking in self-interest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: So it's not just the scholars, it's also the armies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: The armies, and they're looking to gain access and control over resources elsewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: The markets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And hence the imperial imperative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: To conquer, to expand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Although that itself of course is a universal thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I mean, no civilization I think that we know of doesn't try to gain ground from its neighbors

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: where it can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: The Western ability to go further, faster certainly gave an advantage in that regard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Do some civilizations get a bit more excited by that kind of idea than others?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: It's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: But you could say it's the Western civilization because the technological innovation was more

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: efficient, doing that kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: But maybe it wanted it more too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Well the Ottomans wanted it an awful lot and did terribly well for many centuries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: One shouldn't forget that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: As did others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I'd also say by the way, and again it's a very broad one, but it's worth throwing out

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: there, I think self-criticism is an important attribute of the Western mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: One that as you know is not common everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Not all societies allow even their most vociferous critics to become rich.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: So you know, criticism is a negative sounding word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: It could be self-introspection, self-analysis, self-reflection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And it can be what you need.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: You know, and in the Western system I'd argue that one of the advantages of the system of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: representative governance is that where there are problems in the system, you can attempt

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: to sort them out by peaceable means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: We listen to arguments, most famously in America in the late 20th century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: The civil rights movement achieved its aims by force of moral argument and persuaded the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: rest of the country that it had been wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: It's not common in every society by any means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: So I think there are certain attributes to the Western mind that you could say are, they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: not entirely unique, but they are not as commonplace elsewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: What about the emergence in hierarchies of asymmetry of power, most visible, most drastic

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: in the form of slavery, for example?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Well, I mean, everyone in the world is slavery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: I don't regard it as being a unique Western sin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: It's rather hard to think of a civilization in history that didn't have slavery of some

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: kind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: One of the oddities of the Western ignorance of our day is that people seem to imagine

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: that our societies in the West were the only ones who ever engaged in any vices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Alas, this isn't true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: It's a sort of Rousseauian mistake, or at least one that's blossomed since Rousseau,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: that everybody else in the world was born into sort of Edenic innocence and only we

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: in the West had this sort of evil in us that caused us to do bad things to other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Slavery was engaging by everyone in the ancient world, of course, and through most of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: modern world as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Of course, there are 40 million slaves in the world today, so it's clearly not something

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: that the species as a whole has a problem with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: That's more slaves, of course, than there were in the 19th century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And I'd say on top of that, the interesting thing about the Western mind as regards to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: slavery is that we were the civilization that did away with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And by the way, the founding fathers of America who today are lambasted routinely for being

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: acquiescent in the slave trade, engaging in it, owning slaves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: People almost don't even bother now to recognize the facts that Thomas Jefferson, George Washington,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: all wanted to see this trade done away with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Couldn't hold the country together at the origins if they'd have made such an effort

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: and believed and hoped that it would be something that would be dealt with after their time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: So the founding ideas had within them the notion that we should, as a people, get rid

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: The founding lines of the Declaration of Independence set up the conditions under which slavery

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: will be impossible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: All men are created equal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Once you've put that, that's a time bomb under the whole concept of slavery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: That's ticking away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And sure enough, it detonated in the next century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: If we just step back and look at the human species, what does slavery teach you about

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: human nature?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: The fact that slavery has appeared as a function of society throughout human history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: There are two possibilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: One is it's what people think they can do when God's not watching.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Another is it's what they can do if they think that God allows it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Really, really well put.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And the fact that they want to do this kind of subjugation, what does that mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Well, I mean, it's pretty straightforward in a way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: There are people who get to work for free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Because economic in nature in some sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: But in order to do it, I mean, almost always, there are some examples in the ancient world

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: where this wasn't the case, but almost always it had to be a subjugated people or people

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: regarded as different.

body.input: Too personal, far too personal of a question to ask a Brit.

body.input: But what was that like and broadly speaking, what's the role of love in the human condition?

body.input: I'm very perilously personal.

body.input: Rules are meant to be broken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: One of the ways in which growing up and realizing you're gay differs from growing up and being

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Oh wow, I never thought about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Now that's not to say, I mean, there's plenty of unrequited love among young men for young

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: women, young women for young men, plenty of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: because the odds are that the person in question will not be gay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Is heartbreak and disappointment.

body.input: Heartbreak can be beautiful too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: It's formative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Well, again, it comes back to the thing if you're a writer or something, because you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: can always do something with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: that.

body.input: It's dangerous.

body.input: What's the danger in that exactly?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: That seeing the material in the human experience, you don't experience it fully?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: You don't experience it fully and you might be using it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: in the 60s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: thought I could use this for a poem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Anyhow, that's a divergence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Life is full of guilty pleasures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And I think that's one of them because if you feel that guilt, really what you're doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: is you're capturing that moment and you're going to impact the lives of many, many people

body.input: by writing about that moment because it's going to stimulate something that resonates

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: And it means that most, certainly in my generation, most gay men came to sexual or romantic maturity

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: later.

body.input: So what's the meaning is a hard one, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: useful than any others because the conservative answer is find meaning where people have found

body.input: it before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: Which is a very, very good answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Murray: Racism, Marxism, and the War on the West | Lex Fridman Podcast #296

body.input: it's...

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: As a side note, let me say that our little sun is orbited by not just a few planets in the planetary

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: region, but trillions of objects in the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud that extends over three

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: light years out. This to me is amazing, since Proxima Centauri, the closest star to our sun,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: is only 4.2 light years away. And all of it is mostly covered in darkness. When I get a chance

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: to go out swimming in the ocean far from the shore, I'm sometimes overcome by the terrifying

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: and the exciting feeling of not knowing what's there in the deep darkness. That's how I feel

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: about the edge of our solar system. One day, I hope humans will travel there. Or at the very least,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: AI systems that carry the flame of human consciousness. This is the Lux Freebin Podcast,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: and here's my conversation with Kostantin Batygin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: What is Planet Nine? Planet Nine is an object that we believe lives in the solar system beyond the

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: orbit of Neptune. It orbits the sun with a period of about 10,000 years and is about five Earth

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: masses. So that's a hypothesized object. There's some evidence for this kind of object. There's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: bunch of different explanations. Can you give like an overview of the planets and how they

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: the planets in our solar system, how many are there? What do we know and not know about them

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: at a high level? All right. That sounds like a good plan. So look, the solar system

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: basically is comprised of two parts, the inner and the outer solar system. The inner solar system

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: has the planets Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars. Now Mercury is about 40% of the orbital separation

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: of where the Earth is. It's closer to the sun. Venus is about 70%. Then Mars is about 160%

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: further away from the sun than is the Earth. These planets that we, one of them we occupy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: right, are pretty small. They're two leading order sort of heavily overgrown asteroids, if you will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Okay. This becomes evident when you move out further in the solar system and encounter Jupiter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: which is 316 Earth masses, right, 10 times the size. Saturn is another huge one. 90 Earth masses

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: at about 10 times the separation from the sun as is the Earth. Then you have Uranus and Neptune

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: at 20 and 30 respectively. For a long time, that is where the kind of massive part of the solar

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: system ended. But what we've learned in the last 30 years is that beyond Neptune, there's this

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: expansive field of icy debris, a second icy asteroid belt in the solar system. A lot of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: have heard of the asteroid belt, which lives between Mars and Jupiter, right? That's a pretty

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: common thing that people like to imagine and draw on lunch boxes and stuff. But beyond Neptune,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: there's a much more massive and much more radially expansive field of debris. Pluto, by the way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: it belongs to that second icy asteroid belt, which we call the Kuiper belt. It's just a big object

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: within that population of bodies. Pluto, the planet. Pluto, the dwarf planet, the former planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Why is Pluto not a planet anymore? I mean, it's tiny. We used to-

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: The size matters when it comes to planets. Oh, 100%. It's actually a fascinating story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: When Pluto was discovered in 1930, the reason it was discovered in the first place is because

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: astronomers at the time were looking for a seven Earth mass planet somewhere beyond Neptune. It was

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: hypothesized that such an object exists. When they found something, they interpreted that as a seven

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Earth mass planet and immediately revised its mass downward because they couldn't resolve the object

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: with the telescope. So it looked like just a point mass star rather than a physical disk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: They said, well, maybe it's not seven, maybe it's one. Then over the next, I guess, 40 years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Pluto's mass kept getting revised downwards, downwards, downwards until it was realized that

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: it's like 500 times less massive than the Earth. I mean, Pluto's surface area is almost perfectly

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: equal to the surface area of Russia, actually. Russia is big, but it's not a planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Well, I mean, actually we can touch more on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: That's another discussion. So in some sense, earlier in the century, Pluto represented

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: our ignorance about the edges of the solar system. And perhaps Planet Nine is the thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: that represents our ignorance about now the modern set of ignorances about the edges of

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: our solar system. That's a good way to put it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: By the way, just imagining this belt of astro of debris at the edge of our solar system is

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: incredible. Can you talk about it a little bit? What is the Kuiper belt and what is the Oort cloud?

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Yeah. Okay. So look, the simple way to think about it is that if you imagine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: you know, Neptune's orbit like a circle, right? Kind of maybe a factor of one and a half, 1.3 times bigger

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: on a radius of 1.3 times bigger, you've got a whole collection of icy objects. Most of these objects

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: are sort of the size of Austin, you know, maybe a little bit smaller. If you then zoom out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: right, and explore the orbits of the most long period Kuiper belt object, these are the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: that have the biggest orbits and take the longest time to go around the sun. Then what you find is

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: that beyond a critical orbit size, beyond a critical orbit period, which is about 4,000 years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: you start to see weird structure, like all the orbits sort of point into one direction. And all

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: the orbits are kind of tilted in the same way by about 20 degrees with respect to sun. This is

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: particularly pronounced in orbits that are not heavily affected by Neptune. So there you start

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: to see this weird dichotomy where there are objects which are stable, which Neptune does not mess with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: gravitationally, and unstable objects. The unstable objects are basically all over the place

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: because they're being kicked around by Neptune. The stable orbits show this remarkable pattern

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: of clustering. We, back I guess five years ago, interpreted this pattern of clustering as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: gravitational one-way sign, the existence of a planet in a distant planet, right, something that

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: is shepherding and confining these orbits together. Of course, right, you have to have some skepticism

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: when you're talking about these things. You have to ask the question of, okay, how statistically

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: significant is this clustering? And there are many authors that have indeed called that into question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: We have done our own analyses. And basically, just like with all statistics where there's kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: multiple ways to do the exercise, you can either ask the question of, if I have a telescope that has

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: surveyed this part of the sky, what are the chances that I would discover this clustering?

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: That basically tells you that you have zero confidence, right? That does not give you

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: a confident answer one way or another. Another way to do the statistics, which is what we prefer

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: to do, is to say, we have a whole night sky of discoveries in the Kuiper belt, right? And if we

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: have some object over there, which has right ascension and declination, which is a way to say

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: it's there on the sky, and it has some brightness, that means somebody looked over there and

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: discovered an object of, was able to discover an object of that brightness or brighter. Through

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: that analysis, you can construct a whole map on the sky of kind of where all of the surveys that

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: have ever been done have collectively looked. So if you do the exercise this way, the false alarm

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: probability of the clustering on which the Planet Nine hypothesis is built is about 0.4%.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Wow. Okay. So there's a million questions here. One, when you say bright objects, why are they

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: bright? Are we talking about actual objects within the Kuiper belt or the stuff we see through the

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Kuiper belt? This is the actual stuff we see in the Kuiper belt. The way you go about discovering

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Kuiper belt objects, pretty easy. I mean, it's easy in theory, right? Hard in practice. All you

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: do is you take snapshots of the sky, right? Choose that object, and you can do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Snapshots of the sky, right? Choose that direction and take the high exposure snapshot. Then you

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: wait a night and you do it again, and then you wait another night and you do it again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Objects that are just random stars in the galaxy don't move on the sky, whereas objects in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: solar system will slowly move. This is no different than if you're driving down the freeway,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: it looks like trees are going by you faster than the clouds, right? This is parallax.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: That's it. It's just they're reflecting light off of the sun, and it's going back and hitting this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: There's a little bit of a glimmer from the different objects that you can see based on

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: the reflection from the sun. So there's actual light, it's not darkness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: That's right. These are just big icicles basically that are just reflecting sunlight back at you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: It's then easy to understand why it's so hard to discover them because light has to travel to

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: something like 40 times the distance between the earth and the sun and then get reflected back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Was that like an hour travel?

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Yeah, that's right. That's something like that because the earth to the sun is eight minutes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: I believe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: And so something, you know, hours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Yeah, in that order of magnitude. So that's interesting. So you have to account for all of

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: that. And then there's a huge amount of data, pixels that are coming from the pictures. And you

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: have to integrate all of that together to paint a sort of like a high estimate of the different

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: objects. Can you track them? Can you be like, that's Bob? Like, can you like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Yes, exactly. In fact, one of them is named Joe Biden. I mean, I'm not like this is not even a joke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Is there a Trump one or no?

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: No, no. I don't know. I haven't seen that one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: I haven't checked for that. But like, the way it works is if you discover one, you right away get a

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: license plate for it. OK, so like the first four numbers is the first year that this object has

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: appeared on, you know, in the data set, if you will. And then there's like this code that follows

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: it, which basically tells you where in the sky it is. Right. So one of the really interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Kuiper Belt objects, which is very much part of the Planet Nine stories called VP 113,

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: because Joe Biden was vice president at the time, you know, got nicknamed Biden.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: VP 113, you said?

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: He got nicknamed Biden. Beautiful. What's the fingerprint for any particular object? Like, how

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: do you know it's the same one? Or you just kind of like, yeah, from night to night, you take a

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: picture. How do you know it's the same object? Yeah. So the way you know is it appears in almost

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: exactly the same part of the sky except for moves. But this is why actually you need at least three

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: nights, because oftentimes asteroids, which are much closer to the Earth, like will appear

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: to move only slightly, but then on the third night will move away. So that third night is really

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: there to detect acceleration. Now, the thing that I didn't really realize until, you know, I started

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: observing together with my partner in crime in all this, Mike Brown, is just the fact that for the

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: first year when you make these detections, the only thing you really know with confidence is where it

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: is on the night sky and how far away it is. Okay? That's it. You don't know anything about the orbit

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: because over three days, the object just moves so little, right? That whole motion on the sky is

metadata.title: Podcast: Konstantin Batygin: Planet 9 and the Edge of Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #201

body.input: entirely coming from motion of the Earth, right? So the Earth is kind of the car, the object is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: which is kind of mad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: Yeah, yeah. So what happened? So this is what I think it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: Yeah, it's fascinating. I mean, Daniel Kahnema talks about this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: that most of our life is lived in our memories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: So maybe free will exists in imagination. Choices are made in your imagination.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: because you're like, imagining, like reinterpreting constantly the things that happen to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: signal? I think we have an obsession with making contact with events. So what I mean by that is

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: feeling, but the discussion right now is sort of at the level of modern mythology. Aliens are our

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: things that we traditionally only regularize through mythology actually become things that

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

metadata.title: Podcast: Alien Debate: Sara Walker and Lee Cronin | Lex Fridman Podcast #279

body.input: Would you make the myth, would you give credit to the myth, the mythology as first contact?
