metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Now we've disrupted the entire vacuuming industry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: The number one selling vacuums, for example, in the US,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: are Roombas, so not robot vacuums, but vacuums,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and that's really crazy and weird.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We need to pause that. I mean, that's incredible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: That's incredible that a robot is the number one selling thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that does something, something as essential as vacuuming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Congratulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Thank you. It's still kind of fun to say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but just because this was a crazy idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that just started in a room here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: we were like, do you think we can do this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So, hey, let's give it a try.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But now the robots are starting to understand their environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And if you think about the next step, there's two dimensions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I've been working so hard since the beginning of iRobot

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to make robots are autonomous, that they're smart enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and understand their task enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that they can just go do it without human involvement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Now what I'm really excited and working on

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: is how do I make them less autonomous,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: meaning that the robot is supposed to be your partner,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: not this automaton that just goes and does what a robot does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so that if you tell it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: hey, I just dropped some flour by the fridge in the kitchen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Can you deal with it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Wouldn't it be awesome if the right thing just happened

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: based on that utterance?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And to some extent, that's less autonomous

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: because it's actually listening to you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: understanding the context and intent of the sentence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: mapping it against its understanding of the home it lives in

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and knowing what to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so that's an area of research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It's an area where we're starting to roll out features.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: You can now tell your robot to clean up the kitchen,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and it knows what the kitchen is and can do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And that's sort of 1.0 of where we're going.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: The other cool thing is that we're starting to know where stuff is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And why is that important?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Well, robots are supposed to have arms, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Data had an arm, Rosie had an arm, Robbie the robot had an arm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I mean, robots are, you know, they are physical things

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that move around in an environment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and they're supposed to like do work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And if you think about it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: if a robot doesn't know where anything is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: why should it have an arm?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But with this new dawn of home understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that we're starting to go enjoy, I know where the kitchen is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I might in the future know where the refrigerator is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I might, if I had an arm, be able to find the handle,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: open it, and even get myself a beer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Obviously, that's one of the true dreams of robotics

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: is to have robots bringing us a beer while we watch television.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But I think that that new category of tasks

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: where physical manipulation, robot arms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: is just a potpourri of new opportunity and excitement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And you see humans as a crucial part of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So you kind of mentioned that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and I personally find that a really compelling idea, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Full autonomy can only take us so far, especially in the home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So you see humans as helping the robot understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: or give deeper meaning to the spatial information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Right. It's a partnership.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: The robot is supposed to operate according to descriptors

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that you would use to describe your own home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: The robot is supposed to, in lieu of better direction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: kind of go about its routine, which ought to be basically right

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and lead to a home maintained in a way that it's learned you like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but also be perpetually ready to take direction

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that would activate a different set of behaviors or actions

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to meet a current need to the extent it could actually perform that task.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So I've got to ask you, I think this is a fundamental and fascinating question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: because iRobot has been a successful company

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and a rare successful robotics company.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So Anki, Jibo, Mayfield Robotics with their robot, Kuri,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Sci-Fi Works, Rethink Robotics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: these are robotics companies that were founded and run by brilliant people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But all very unfortunately, at least for us roboticists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: all went out of business recently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So why do you think they didn't last longer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Why do you think it is so hard to keep a robotics company alive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: You know, I say this only partially in jest

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that back in the day before Roomba,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: you know, I was a high tech entrepreneur building robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But it wasn't until I became a vacuum cleaner salesman that we had any success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So, I mean, the point is technology alone doesn't equal a successful business.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We need to go and find the compelling need

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: where the robot that we're creating can deliver clearly more value

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to the end user than it costs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And this is not a marginal thing where you're looking at the skin like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: it's close, maybe we can hold our breath and make it work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It's clearly more value than the cost of the robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to bring in the store.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And I think that the challenge has been finding those businesses

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: where that's true in a sustainable fashion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: You know, when you get into entertainment style things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: you could be the cat's meow one year,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but 85% of toys, regardless of their merit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: fail to make it to their second season.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It's just super hard to do so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so that's just a tough business.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And there's been a lot of experimentation around

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: what is the right type of social companion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: what is the right robot in the home that is doing something

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: other than tasks people do every week that they'd rather not do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And I'm not sure we've got it all figured out right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so that you get brilliant roboticists with super interesting robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that ultimately don't quite have that magical user experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and thus that value benefit equation remains ambiguous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So you as somebody who dreams of robots changing the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: what's your estimate?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: How big is the space of applications that fit the criteria

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that you just described where you can really demonstrate

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: an obvious significant value over the alternative non-robotic solution?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Well, I think that we're just about none of the way

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to achieving the potential of robotics at home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But we have to do it in a really eyes wide open, honest fashion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Another way to put that is the potential is infinite

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: because we did take a few steps,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but you're saying those steps are just very initial steps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So the Roomba is a hugely successful product,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but you're saying that's just the very, very beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: That's just the very, very beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It's the foot in the door.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And I think I was lucky that in the early days of robotics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: people would ask me, when are you going to clean my floor?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It was something that I grew up saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I got all these really good ideas,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but everyone seems to want their floor clean.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so maybe we should do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Yeah, your good ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Earn the right to do the next thing after that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So the good ideas have to match with the desire of the people

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and then the actual cost has to, like the business,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: the financial aspect has to all match together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Yeah, during our partnership back a number of years ago

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: with Johnson Wax, they would explain to me

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that they would go into homes and just watch how people lived

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and try to figure out what were they doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that they really didn't really like to do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but they had to do it frequently enough that it was top of mind

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and understood as a burden.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Hey, let's make a product or come up with a solution

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to make that pain point less challenging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And sometimes we do certain burdens so often as a society

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that we actually don't even realize,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: like it's actually hard to see that that burden is something

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that could be removed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So it does require just going into the home and staring at,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: wait, how do I actually live life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: What are the pain points?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Yeah, and getting those insights is a lot harder

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: than it would seem it should be in retrospect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So how hard on that point, I mean, one of the big challenges

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: of robotics is driving the cost to something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: driving the cost down to something that consumers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: people would afford.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So people would be less likely to buy a Roomba

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: if it cost $500,000, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Which is probably sort of what a Roomba would cost

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: several decades ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So how do you drive, which I imagine is very difficult,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: how do you drive the cost of a Roomba or a robot down

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: such that people would want to buy it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: When I started building robots, the cost of the robot had a lot

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to do with the amount of time it took to build it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so that we would build our robots out of aluminum,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I would go spend my time in the machine shop

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: on the milling machine, cutting out the parts and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And then when we got into the toy industry,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I realized that if we were building at scale,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I could determine the cost of the robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: instead of adding up all the hours to mill out the parts,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but by weighing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And that's liberating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: You can say, wow, the world has just changed

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: as I think about construction in a different way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: The 3D CAD tools that are available to us today,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: the operating at scale where I can do tooling

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and injection mold, an arbitrarily complicated part,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and the cost is going to be basically the weight

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: of the plastic in that part,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: is incredibly exciting and liberating

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and opens up all sorts of opportunities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And for the sensing part of it, where we are today is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: instead of trying to build skin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: which is really hard, for a long time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I spent creating strategies and ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: around how could we duplicate the skin on the human body,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: because it's such an amazing sensor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Instead of going down that path,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: why don't we focus on vision

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and how many of the problems that face a robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: trying to do real work could be solved

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: with a cheap camera and a big ass computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And Moore's Law continues to work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: The cell phone industry, the mobile industry

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: is giving us better and better tools

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that can run on these embedded computers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And I think we passed an important moment

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: maybe two years ago where you could put

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: machine vision capable processors on robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: at consumer price points.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And I was waiting for it to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We had avoided putting lasers on our robots to do navigation

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and instead spent years researching

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: how to do vision-based navigation

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: because you could just see where these technology trends were going.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And between injection molded plastic

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and a camera with a computer capable of running machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and visual object recognition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I could build an incredibly affordable, incredibly capable robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and that's going to be the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: On that point with a small tangent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but I think an important one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: another industry in which I would say the only other industry

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: in which there is automation actually touching people's lives today

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: is autonomous vehicles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: What the vision you just described of using computer vision

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and using cheap camera sensors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: there's a debate on that of lidar versus computer vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And sort of the Elon Musk famously said that lidar is a crutch

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that really in camera in the long term,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: camera only is the right solution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: which echoes some of the ideas you're expressing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Of course, the domain in terms of its safety criticality is different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But what do you think about that approach in the autonomous vehicle space?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And in general, do you see a connection between

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: the incredible real world challenges you have to solve in the home with Roomba?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I saw a demonstration of some of them, corner cases literally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and autonomous vehicles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So there's absolutely a tremendous overlap between both the problems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: you know, a robot vacuum and autonomous vehicle are trying to solve,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and the tools and the types of sensors that are being applied

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: in the pursuit of the solutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: In my world, my environment is actually much harder

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: than the environment in automobile travels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We don't have roads. We have t-shirts. We have steps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We have a near infinite number of patterns and colors

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and surface textures on the floor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Especially from a visual perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Visually it looks really tough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It's an infinitely variable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: On the other hand, safety is way easier on the inside.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: My robots, they're not very heavy. They're not very fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: If they bump into your foot, you think it's funny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And autonomous vehicles kind of have the inverse problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so that for me saying vision is the future,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I can say that without reservation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: For autonomous vehicles, I think I believe what Elon's saying

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: about the future is ultimately going to be vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Maybe if we put a cheap lighter on there as a backup sensor,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: it might not be the worst idea in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So the stakes are much higher.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: You have to be much more careful thinking through how far away that future is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But I think that the primary environmental understanding sensor

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: is going to be a visual system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Visual system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So on that point, well, let me ask,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: do you hope there's an iRobot robot in every home in the world one day?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I expect there to be at least one iRobot robot in every home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We've sold 25 million robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So we're in about 10% of US homes, which is a great start.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But I think that when we think about the numbers of things that robots can do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: today I can vacuum your floor, mop your floor, cut your lawn,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: or soon we'll be able to cut your lawn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But there are more things that we could do in the home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And I hope that we continue using the techniques I described

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: around exploiting computer vision and low-cost manufacturing

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that will be able to create these solutions at affordable price points.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So let me ask, on that point of a robot in every home, that's my dream as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I'd love to see that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I think the possibilities there are indeed infinite positive possibilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But in our current culture, no thanks to science fiction and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: there's a serious kind of hesitation, anxiety, concern about robots,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and also a concern about privacy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And it's a fascinating question to me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: why that concern amongst a certain group of people is as intense as it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So you have to think about it because it's a serious concern,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: but I wonder how you address it best.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So from a perspective of a vision sensor,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: so robots that move about the home and sense the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: how do you alleviate people's privacy concerns?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: How do you make sure that they can trust iRobot

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and the robots that they share their home with?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I think that's a great question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We've really leaned way forward on this because given our vision

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: as to the role the company intends to play in the home,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: really for us, make or break is can our approach be trusted

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to protecting the data and the privacy of the people who have our robots?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so we've gone out publicly with a privacy manifesto

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: stating we'll never sell your data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We've adopted GDPR not just where GDPR is required, but globally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We have ensured that images don't leave the robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So processing data from the visual sensors happens locally on the robot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and only semantic knowledge of the home with the consumer's consent is sent up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We show you what we know and are trying to go use data as an enabler

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: for the performance of the robots with the informed consent

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and understanding of the people who own those robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And we take it very seriously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And ultimately, we think that by showing a customer that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: if you let us build a semantic map of your home and know where the rooms are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: well, then you can say, clean the kitchen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: If you don't want the robot to do that, don't make the map.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It'll do its best job cleaning your home, but it won't be able to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And if you ever want us to forget that we know that it's your kitchen,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: you can have confidence that we will do that for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So we're trying to go and be a sort of a data 2.0 perspective company

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: where we treat the data that the robots have of the consumer's home

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: as if it were the consumer's data and that they have rights to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So we think by being the good guys on this front,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: we can build the trust and thus be entrusted to enable robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to do more things that are thoughtful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Do you think people's worries will diminish over time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: As a society, broadly speaking, do you think you can win over trust

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: not just for the company, but just the comfort that people have

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: with AI in their home enriching their lives in some way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I think we're in an interesting place today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We're less about winning them over and more about finding a way

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to talk about privacy in a way that more people can understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I would tell you that today, when there's a privacy breach,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: people get very upset and then go to the store and buy the cheapest thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: paying no attention to whether or not the products that they're buying

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: are on our privacy standards or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: In fact, if I put on the package of my Roomba,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: the privacy commitments that we have, I would sell less than I would

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: if I did nothing at all, and that needs to change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So it's not a question about earning trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I think that's necessary but not sufficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: We need to figure out how to have a comfortable set of what is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: grade A meet standard applied to privacy that customers can trust

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and understand and then use in their buying decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: That will reward companies for good behavior,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and that will ultimately be how this moves forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And maybe be part of the conversation between regular people

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: about what it means, what privacy means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: If you have some standards, you can say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: you're going to start talking about who's following them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: who's not, have more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Because most people are actually quite clueless about all aspects

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: of artificial intelligence, of data collection, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It would be nice to change that for people to understand the good that AI can do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and it's not some system that's trying to steal all the most sensitive data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Yep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Do you think, do you dream of a Roomba with human-level intelligence one day?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So you've mentioned a very successful localization and mapping of the environment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: being able to do some basic communication to say, go clean the kitchen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Do you see in your maybe more bored moments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: once you get the beer, just sit back with that beer

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and have a chat on a Friday night with the Roomba about how your day went?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So to your latter question, absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: To your former question as to whether a robot can have human-level intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: not in my lifetime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I think you can have a great conversation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: a meaningful conversation with a robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: without it having anything that resembles human-level intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And I think that as long as you realize that conversation is not about the robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and making the robot feel good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: That conversation is about you learning interesting things

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that make you feel like the conversation that you had with the robot is

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: a pretty awesome way of learning something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And it could be about what kind of day your pet had.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It could be about how can I make my home more energy efficient?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: It could be about if I'm thinking about climbing Mount Everest, what should I know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And that's a very doable thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: But if I think that that conversation I'm going to have with the robot is

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I'm going to be rewarded by making the robot happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I could just put a button on the robot that you could push and the robot would smile

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and that sort of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: So I think you need to think about the question in the right way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And robots can be awesomely effective at helping people feel less isolated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: learn more about the home that they live in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and fill some of those lonely gaps that we wish we were engaged

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: learning cool stuff about our world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Last question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: If you could hang out for a day with a robot from science fiction, movies, books,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: and safely pick its brain for that day, who would you pick?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: From Star Trek.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I think that A, data is really smart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Data has been through a lot trying to go and save the galaxy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And I'm really interested actually in emotion and robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And I think he'd have a lot to say about that because I believe actually that

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: emotion plays an incredibly useful role in doing reasonable things in situations

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: where we have imperfect understanding of what's going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: In social situations when there's imperfect information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: In social situations, also in competitive or dangerous situations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: that we have emotion for a reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so that ultimately my theory is that as robots get smarter and smarter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: they're actually going to get more emotional because you can't actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: survive on pure logic because only a very tiny fraction of the situations

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: we find ourselves in can be resolved reasonably with logic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so I think Data would have a lot to say about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: And so I could find out whether he agrees.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: What if you could ask Data one question that you would get a deep honest answer

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: to what would you ask?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: What's Captain Picard really like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Okay, I think that's the perfect way to end it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: Colin, thank you so much for talking today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: I really appreciate it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Colin Angle: iRobot CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #39

body.input: My pleasure.

body.input: of human nature. Please let me also address something for a few minutes that happened recently

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: about Bitcoin and life in general for three hours. I was curious, inspired, positive, or at least I

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: tried to be as I usually do. Someone clipped out, out of context, a short segment of me mumbling

body.input: something about having a PhD and I started getting mocked online because that made it

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: convenient for people to mock me for being yet another quote unquote expert who learns about

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Bitcoin and thinks he knows everything. I almost never mentioned that I have a PhD except to make

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: fun of myself as I was doing or at least trying to do in the full context of that conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I brought up grad school as a random example of one of the many journeys I've taken that was hard

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: but where the destination was in itself not very useful. I was saying I enjoy exploring with a

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: curious mind and I'm willing to be patient, to learn, to listen, to humble myself with knowledge

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: for the sake of knowledge itself. Grad school was an example of that. The PhD means nothing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: at least to me. I never call myself an expert or at least try not to because that would be dumb

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: because I know how little I know. I'm not a influencer or a thought leader or whatever else

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: silly self aggrandizing label people put on their LinkedIn. I try to be the opposite of what I was

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: mocked for. I try to think deeply about the world, to look for the beautiful ideas in the minds of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: others and to be inspired by them. I wanted to say all this because psychologically it struck a bit

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: of a blow. It made me realize that even when I approach things with love I may be mocked,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I may be derided, I may be taken out of context or even lied about. With the growing platform this

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: is sadly only increasing. I now have learned that there's people who are waiting for my missteps

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: so they can point the finger, laugh and say, see I told you so, that guy's a joke, he's a fraud.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: As a fellow human being the knowledge of this is painful. Yes, I know people tell me to toughen up

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and my life has been about strengthening my mind in the face of my limits, but I refuse to not be

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: fragile and wear my heart on my sleeve. It's who I am. In some sense this is the immune system of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: the internet, but let us be careful not to destroy the good ones in the process. The Bitcoin community

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: had to endure many years of attacks from quote unquote experts and also fraudulent cryptocurrency

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: efforts that scam people out of their money. This created a powerful immune system that fought the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: attackers and the scammers. I understand this and I also understand that one of the beautiful aspects

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: of Bitcoin is its community of humans is decentralized. But some small part of this

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: community has come to enjoy the us versus them battles, sometimes for the sake of the battle in

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: itself. This happens in political discourse as well. I understand this, but to my limited mind

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: it sounds like groupthink, which has powerful defense mechanisms against bad ideas, but has

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: dangerous consequences if taken too far. As in many periods of human history that I often talk about

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: where the us versus them thinking has led to the suffering of many. Again, I understand the value

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: of this as many Bitcoin is explained to me, but it's not the way I as a sovereign individual choose

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: to walk in this life. By the way, none of this podcast should be treated as financial advice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Before Nick kindly gifted me with a hundred dollars worth of Bitcoin in hardware form,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I didn't own any. I'll probably buy some Bitcoin on Cash App, Coinbase and other platforms and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: also transfer to a hardware wallet just to learn how to do it. But other than that, I don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: necessarily make wise investment decisions. Money is not a motivation for me personally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I try to avoid it actually. I'm grateful for every day I'm alive no matter how much money is in my

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: bank account. For long stretches of my life, that number was very close to zero and I was always

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: fortunate to be free and happy. So I encourage you to listen to people much smarter than me

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: for actual good financial advice. Here I'm just exploring ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And as if this has not already gone on too long, let me please make another comment on the style

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: of discourse among some Bitcoin maximalists on platforms like Twitter. That in my humble view,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I may be wrong, but I believe is not conducive to the nuanced empathetic exchange of ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I very much look for and enjoy. Again, I appreciate their style of discourse. I think I understand the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: value of it, but it's not my thing. So I don't want to engage in it. I want to hear the quiet

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: voices in the room. I look for people to inspire each other. And when we disagree, I look for

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: disagreement that is grounded in respect and empathy. I think that mockery and derision

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: destroys the possibility of those nuanced conversations. It drives away the quiet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: thoughtful, empathetic voices. And I try to give those voices space to be heard, to shine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: to exchange ideas, whether we agree or disagree. So if I happen to block you on Twitter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I block you with love. Honestly, I will never speak poorly of you or even think poorly of you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I would love to hang out in person, give you a big old hug, and talk about life over some beers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: If you see or hear me say something stupid, which I'm sure I do often, or something you disagree

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: with, and you still respect me as a human being, please show your love as I always do to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But also send me some links to blogs, books, videos, podcasts, where people describe why

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: my stated idea may be totally wrong. I love this kind of long-form disagreement. I humble myself

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: every day by reading books and blogs by people much smarter than me. Sometimes it strengthens

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: my ideas, sometimes it totally changes them. But I always learn. This is a too long way of saying

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: that I'm here trying to walk with grace and with an open mind, a bit of patience, and always love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: If I make mistakes, cut me some slack. Like you, I'm only human. Allegedly.

body.input: What philosopher or philosophical idea had a big impact on your life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: not just in the space of cryptocurrency, but in general?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Oh, so we're going now. We're rolling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: We're going right in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: We're rolling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Because you majored in philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I did. I majored in philosophy. I didn't know what to do with my life, and my parents said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: do whatever you find interesting. It's like, okay, philosophy, great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I find that interesting. And it had way more of an impact on my career actually than I thought it

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: might. Typically, I guess if you do philosophy, you go into a lot of finance, so it makes sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But there are a number of philosophers I really admire. One of my favorites would be Descartes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: probably the notion of skepticism. It's sort of a rabbit hole. It's kind of hard to pull yourself

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: out of it. Basically, the brain in the vat theory, pulling yourself out of that. But yeah,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I really like epistemology, questioning what it is to have knowledge. So Descartes was one of my

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: gateways to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Do you think everything is knowable? We humans can know fully the objective reality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Oh, definitely not. No, I mean, reality is very much processed through your own subjective

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: lens. So how much do you think do we understand about this world? Because a lot of your ideas,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: a lot of things we might talk about today are kind of trying to figure out human civilization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: how human behavior works at scale, all those kinds of things. That kind of assumes that we have it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: or we're able to somehow figure most of it out. So when you step way back, you're going to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: step way back. How much of it have we really figured out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Well, I think that's the conceit of economics is thinking that you can model human behavior

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: in these unbelievably complex systems. And then I think that's the modern critique of economics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: like the sort of Taliban critique is that you can't have true knowledge, and they're much less

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: predictable than we think they are. And we behave according to our accumulated assumptions, and we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: using tiny sort of data sets trained on the last 50, 100 years. And they turn out to be horribly

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: askew. And that's when we have our gray swans and our black swans. So I'm much more on the sort of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: you know, reality is much less noble than we think side of things. But it is nice to have very

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: concrete things like Bitcoin, that's for sure. Oh, so you think so most of it is shaky ground,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: but there's some things there's like islands of sturdiness. Yeah, Bitcoin is one of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's a good way to put it. Yeah. I mean, like, look at the dollar system, not to pivot this into

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: the dollar right away. But the dollar is like shaky ground. It's the most who truly understands

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: the dollar system. I mean, the totality of it, the euro dollar system, the way that monetary policy

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: interacts with the economy is monetary issuance inflationary. What's the relationship between

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: unemployment and inflation? Even policymakers don't understand these things. Economists don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: seem to understand them. What is inflation? How do you define inflation? None of these things are
