metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: in a state of relative immaturity. So we'll see. In terms of other ideas that are side chains,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: just soft forks of Bitcoin, you've mentioned something about Schnorr and Taproot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: What are your thoughts about this update to Bitcoin in terms of its promise to improve privacy and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: scaling and so on? And what other things are you interested, excited about in terms of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: development of Bitcoin? Well, Schnorr and Taproot, that's the first new protocol upgrade since Segwit

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: in 2017, which was what laid the groundwork for Lightning to be developed basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And Schnorr and Taproot is really the first protocol change in three, almost four years now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So we're very excited about it. Is there something interesting to say technically about what are the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: things that's actually going to improve and maybe on the on the politics side, bringing a protocol

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: change on Bitcoin? What does that actually involve? Yeah, I mean, it's a huge deal because the last

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: time we tried to make a change to the protocol, we had a whole civil war over it. And it was

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: incredibly difficult to get Segwit activated in 2017. And it took all this brinksmanship and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: threats and all these campaigns. And it was this whole thing. Luckily, I think things have quieted

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: down and there's much more consensus that Schnorr and Taproot is a good change to Bitcoin. Everyone

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: generally supports it. But everyone kind of has PTSD over the last time when we tried to change

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Bitcoin. And so we're sort of really dithering over how we actually want to implement it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So it's taking forever because we're trying to set the protocol for how do you change Bitcoin

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: itself? And all of our assumptions went out the window last time. So we're trying to reset and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: decide what is a legitimate way to institute a change to Bitcoin. So that's actually the big

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: question right now. It's not should we implement these changes? We basically all agree that we

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: should. It's a meta question is what's the valid way to implement new changes to Bitcoin? What's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: a way that is scalable in the long term and will last and people will consider credible,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: even if this one isn't controversial at all. So that's where we're at. We're basically debating

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: over how do we implement this change that we all want to get a feeling of how slow Bitcoin

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: governance is and how deliberate it is. Everybody collectively wants the change,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: but we haven't fully agreed on how we're going to put it into Bitcoin. So it's a classic sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Bitcoin situation. But what it is is I mean, Schnorr is an alternative signature scheme. I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: it was encumbered by a patent and it had only just been unencumbered when Satoshi created Bitcoin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I believe. It's a better signature scheme than Elliptic Curves, which is what then ECDSA,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which is what Bitcoin uses. And so it's been long enough that we now trust it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: you know, kind of in cryptography, it's meant to be Lindy. You know, it's sort of you want to test

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: it over time and then it's considered safe to use. So Schnorr has been around for long enough that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: we've decided to rip out ECDSA and insert Schnorr, which is just a different signature scheme,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which is more efficient. And it has better properties. Like if you want to do a multi

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: signature transaction where many people collectively sign in order to permission a spend,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: that would be more efficient in a bytes sense than ECDSA, for instance. So it's pretty incremental.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And then Taproot is all about having transactional conditions that are sort of withheld from final

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: entry onto the blockchain. So it's kind of a way to have more private conditional transactions on

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Bitcoin. So both of them, I would say are incremental changes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Is this an over exaggeration that Schnorr Taproot might improve privacy and scaling,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which is it like at the high level things that people mentioned? Is that just like a dramatic way

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: of trying to frame what's fundamentally an incremental improvement?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yes, but incremental is the word, right? It's not, we're not going to get an order of magnitude

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: enhancement to either privacy or scaling, but we will get a considerable enhancement. But privacy

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and scaling are actually two sides of the same coin because you get more transactional privacy

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: by removing data from the ledger so that there's less metadata for people to surveil and analyze.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that's also how you scale by compressing and being really space efficient with transactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And the more parsimonious you are, the more economically dense each byte that everyone has

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: to retain on the ledger is. And so those are very closely allied concepts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So do you mind if we go through some potential criticisms of Bitcoin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Totally. I spent the last five years tackling these every day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Are the dice the same?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Those two are the same. Yeah, there are three editions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Let's go with the dice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: What do we got?
