body.input: Silk Road.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: What does that mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Silk Road, classic, classic situation. So I mean, that was the darknet marketplace set up by Ross Albrecht.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: In the early days of Bitcoin, that's one of the first killer apps for Bitcoin was being the payments

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: network behind this darknet marketplace and where you'd go to buy drugs and things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so that became associated with Bitcoin. If you remember the press coverage from back then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But over time that faded and it became less of a critique.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So like the critique is that Bitcoin is something you would use for illegal activity, for drugs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: for crimes, all those kinds of things, as opposed to for any kind of legitimate transactions and merchant transactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And today Bitcoin settles 10 billion dollars a day and the vast, vast majority of it is completely legitimate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's just a useful alternative system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But back then, a huge fraction of all Bitcoin transactions were related to the basically illicit marketplaces.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And if you're just tuning in, this incredible tall side of die has 11 common criticisms of Bitcoin that Nick in a genius way has put together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Maybe you could do a couple more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Oh, it was Satoshi something. Satoshi coins. Satoshi coins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: We touched on that early in the episode. What if Satoshi returns and sells all of their coins?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So we don't know for sure how many coins Satoshi actually mined or produced because there's a degree of probabilistic analysis that you would do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's a few, few thousand blocks that were mined by what we think is a single entity in sort of 2009.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so if you add them all up, you get to about a million.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So people think that Satoshi mined a million coins and then they're worried that Satoshi would return and market sell all the coins, thus crushing the price of Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So looking at some of these, no CEO. I think we touched on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: We see we've already hit on the dice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: No merchants. That's no longer true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: We talked about that. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's a scalability one. And I think that one is addressed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: The idea that you're mentioning with the block size debates and the Lightning Network that by adding extra layers on top, you can achieve scalability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's my vision. That's my theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And you can do it in a permissionless and a permissioned way. Like Coinbase is a big Bitcoin exchange.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They provide scalability. They're a financial institution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You can settle up internally on their own database and then periodically settle to Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So they do something like the Lightning Network internally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Something like this, some kind of mechanism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Well, honestly, I'm not sure exactly how it works. They might have that built in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But just generally speaking, institutional scaling is a model for scaling, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Where you could have banks holding Bitcoin and they issue notes against Bitcoin and those are your payments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And then the base layer is the settlement layer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think that's what you're getting with the boiling oceans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: This is like the impact on weather, on the environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So that is a concern that people have in terms of like the proof of work requires that there's a lot of computational resources being used.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that requires a lot of energy and like some large percentage of the world's energy is used to mine Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: How would you respond to that criticism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, I mean, that's been the loudest critique of Bitcoin this year in the press.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: This year, really?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah. So I mean, it's not like a new criticism, but Bitcoin is consuming more energy than ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So as the price rises, the electricity consumption rises.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so we've heard renewed bellyaching over this for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, if you don't believe that Bitcoin is useful, then you're inclined to think that all the energy consumption is a waste.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So it's something that's sort of unrebuttable if you fundamentally contest the validity of the Bitcoin system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So if Bitcoin is like a thing that will take over, will become like the main mechanism of financial transactions or transactions period in the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: then you say, well, the cost of energy use is actually quite low relative to the benefit it provides.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: If you think it's not going to be, if it's just a volatile way to make a little money in the short term,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: you see the energy use as really wasteful. It's totally spurious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah. So then there's no really response, I suppose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I can totally get into the details of Bitcoin's energy mix and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But that's like at a high level what the debate is. It's this normative question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Like, does Bitcoin have an entitlement to consume any of the world's resources?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that's actually where the debate should end much of the time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: because a lot of people fundamentally dispute the validity or usefulness of Bitcoin as a system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so, of course, they're going to consider the energy usage illegitimate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Now, there's a lot of mitigating factors if you think the Bitcoin is potentially a useful system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which is Bitcoin consumes energy in a very peculiar way, which virtually no other industry does,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which is that Bitcoin is a geography-independent buyer of energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which is not how we humans typically consume energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: We need energy to be produced near to population centers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and we need it to be produced corresponding to the peaks and troughs of our consumption,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: because we have to 100% match the demand and the supply at all times, otherwise we have blackouts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So Bitcoin doesn't care about any of that. It just buys energy on a constant basis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so it's indifferent to where it's being produced.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so the consequence of all that is that Bitcoin will buy energy that's otherwise being wasted, basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So it will buy so-called stranded energy assets that would not make it to a population center.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And in fact, most energy produced ultimately does not make it to your socket in your wall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so this is why so much Bitcoin is mined in China, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's not because Chinese industrialists had a special affinity for Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's because the Chinese grid had a massive overabundance of energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: particularly in four provinces, Sichuan, Yunnan, Inner Mongolia, and Xinjiang.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So in those four provinces, those are all pretty distant from major population centers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So because of that, you can't really transport the energy that easily.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so huge amounts of energy are curtailed or basically wasted in all these provinces.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so miners set up shop there because they could mine Bitcoin with the excess energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They could monetize this thing that otherwise was going to go to waste.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So there's things like that which I think mitigate the reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Bitcoin is not really rival with our consumption of electricity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's not depriving anyone of electricity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's mostly these stranded assets that are going into supporting the Bitcoin network.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So maybe let's do a last one since you mentioned China.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: This is China control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So if so much mining is happening in China,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: how do we prevent nation states from controlling much of Bitcoin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, that's the flip side of a large portion of the blocks being mined in China

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: due to this energy feature which I discussed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which is that there's a lot of Chinese miners for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Now the question ultimately is what degree of control do miners have over the Bitcoin system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that was part of the block size debate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, the miners, when we implemented subgraded witness in 2017,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: the miners just didn't want to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Eventually, the users, the regular folks running nodes rebelled

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and basically said, look, we're going to implement this whether or not you do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And it was a threat to the value of Bitcoin because if this threat had gone through,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: it could have split Bitcoin and it would have been really messy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So the miners sort of capitulated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I think the current consensus is that miners do not have unilateral control over Bitcoin

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and that governance is more poised between people that run nodes, developers and miners.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's sort of a triumvirate where neither of them has total control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So that's my current model for control in Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think if you asked a miner, they would tell you they didn't feel that they had sort of unilateral control

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: over Bitcoin either.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Almost as a thought experiment, can I ask you to think about if some of your predictions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: some of your analysis, some of your understanding of Bitcoin is wrong

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: in the following sense where it will not have the impact that you have a vision for it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: that you will not have the scale of impact and perhaps in terms of value,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: you will go to zero to something very low and other cryptocurrency or other financial systems will overtake it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: What would be the reason for that in your mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Like, why might you be wrong?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: If you look back at it in the future, what did you not understand about Bitcoin that will result in that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, that's a great question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think for that to happen, one of two things would have to obtain, one of two things would have to happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: for Bitcoin to just be irrelevant basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Either central banks totally clean up their act and stop engaging in rampant money printing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which I don't expect that to happen anytime soon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, it looks like we're normalizing this new regime of inflation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: you know, per inflation to sort of remediate the debt issues we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So that would be one thing that would make Bitcoin cryptocurrency much less relevant

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: as if everyone becomes totally assured of the soundness of sovereign currencies basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: namely the dollar, like the dollar being the main one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It seems like we're going in completely opposite direction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: but most people seem to be noticing the stirrings of inflation in society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You might have noticed it too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's showing up in commodity prices, lumber prices, in food, obviously in financial assets,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and it'll show up in consumer prices generally soon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But so that would be one way for Bitcoin to basically become irrelevant because it's a dialectical thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Bitcoin is held in opposition to the established monetary regime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So if they completely reform themselves and, you know, the dollar becomes super sound once again

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and the Fed stops tinkering the way they constantly do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: then we wouldn't need cryptocurrency as much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: The other thing would be if a completely superior design for a new sort of state independent monetary system emerged,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: but it's really hard to even imagine how that would come to emerge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And there's good reasons to think that Bitcoin, the conditions of its launch were extremely favorable and hard to replicate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Can you speak to some of those conditions, why it's a unique timing wise moment for Bitcoin to emerge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah. So obviously Bitcoin was born in the depths of the financial crisis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which gives it a nice, nice historical element. But that was kind of a coincidence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Honestly, we know that Satoshi had been working on it earlier in 2017.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: The really special thing about Bitcoin was that it was launched anonymously by an entity

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: that did not seek any glory or credit for what they did and apparently never monetized it at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So they never really moved any of their coins. Satoshi sent one test transaction to Hal Finney,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: who was one of the earliest Bitcoiners. Aside from that, as far as we know, Satoshi never spent any of their coins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So you have this wonderful Promethean quality whereby it's almost self-sacrificial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, it's like this borderline godlike figure in terms of their restraint,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: finds this monetary technology and releases it to the world and pays the price.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They never took advantage of their filthy lucre.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They never recognized any of the $50 billion that they made from Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And Satoshi also didn't assign themselves any privileged access to the coins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Satoshi could have just written in the code, I own 10% of the coins. But they didn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They just mined in the open free market competition like everyone else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's just that Satoshi is an early miner to support the network, accumulate a lot of coins for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But they didn't have any privilege special access.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So that's one thing that's extremely special about the launch is that we had a founder

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: that was truly committed to the monetary protocol and didn't seek either recognition or financial spoils.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And then also left, you know, Satoshi left in 2010, 2011 and hasn't really been heard from since.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's a very George Washington gangster move where he didn't want power and once he got power, he let go of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Precisely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That was a key actually move. That was probably one of the most important moves at the founding of this country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's right. George Washington could have been a king, probably if he'd wanted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And Satoshi could have been Jerome Powell if he'd wanted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And Satoshi could have held on to power indefinitely, but chose to leave.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: The other thing is that Bitcoin circulated for a long period of time from January 2009 to about July 2010 without really having a financial value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So there weren't really any marketplaces. It didn't have a value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so that gave it this really great distribution among a broad set of stakeholders.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And there were no venture funds or hedge funds trying to aggressively buy up all the supply back then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Now, when you have new cryptocurrencies launched, they're aggressively pre-mined and some gigantic Silicon Valley venture fund is going to own 30% of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so it's sort of impossible to conceive of how that could become a global money because how could,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: you know, a Silicon Valley investment firm own 30% of the money supply? That doesn't make sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's just so oligarchical, right? It's unbelievable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So Bitcoin by contracts is a very bottom-up thing. It was the early enthusiasts, people that were really excited about the technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They're the ones that obtained those early coins. And so there was a real element of fairness and just an organic nature to its launch, which would be incredibly hard to recapture today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Let's say Satoshi came back and they said, okay, I made Bitcoin 2.0. I'm going to release it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There would be the most aggressive land grab ever by gigantic pools of capital to sort of get favorable allocations of the new system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Right. Can Satoshi with Bitcoin 2.0 build in a resistance mechanism or a prevention mechanism for the land grab?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It would be hard to because, you know, if you have capital and resources, I mean, if it was a proof of work chain, you just have people that would invest a ton of money in mining, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But most new blockchains, cryptocurrencies are just sold. Basically, they're issued in token offerings kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So it's hard to enforce through the protocol the decentralization of control power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, it'd be challenging too. And people have tried to do airdrops, you know, where they distribute coins to a large number of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Basically, it doesn't work. Most people don't care about the airdrop. So it's hard to have an equitable distribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think the conditions of Bitcoin's launch were so lucky and favorable that they're very unlikely to be replicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I do think it's going to be a real challenge to ever have a new competitor that's as decentralized, as leaderless, as dispersed, sort of distributed as Bitcoin has its credibility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I don't know how you could overrule it on those important features.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: What about Bitcoin's comparison to other current cryptocurrencies? So Bitcoin versus Ethereum, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Why is it possible that Ethereum overtakes Bitcoin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's certainly possible. Yeah, I'm not ruling it out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Ethereum leadership is sort of wise enough to understand that they shouldn't compete with Bitcoin on those most profound qualities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Like Ethereum doesn't really aspire to be more sound from a monetary perspective than Bitcoin, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: In fact, the Ethereum leadership are sort of constantly tweaking the monetary policy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So they went for a completely different trade off, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They also don't compete to be as decentralized from a governance perspective, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Because there's leadership. There's an ETH foundation. There's a charismatic leader of Italic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And Ethereum has this policy of hard forks. So in Bitcoin, hard forks are extremely rare.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: In Ethereum, it's the default way to change things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So it's a much more adaptive system and it changes more frequently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But that also means that they're incurring more risk when they introduce those changes. There's much more complexity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So Ethereum is smart because they sort of understood Bitcoin as the top dog when it comes to a sound money, a digital gold type thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And they went for all of the different trade offs. They wanted to be more of a platform.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They wanted to have more complexity at the transactional layer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They wanted to take on more risk in terms of changing the protocol. They wanted to change more quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They wanted to make the monetary policy more mutable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So Ethereum takes that completely different tack.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Of course, I'm not ruling out that it could take over Bitcoin from a market cap perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's just a very different system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And I tend to think that Bitcoin is the most disruptive one because it's the most equipped to challenge sovereign currencies in the grand scheme.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Do you think they can coexist?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So like in the future, do you see a world where Ethereum captures some large percent of the market but nevertheless the minority?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: 100%. Bitcoin has already been tokenized and put onto Ethereum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Many units of Bitcoin, I think over a billion dollars worth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So not only do they coexist, they are actually mutualistic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So they're like two creatures that have this, you know, it's like the rhino and like the bird that pecks the parasites off the rhino's back or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah. Right. So I don't know which is which in the analogy, but I don't know who the parasites are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Or, you know, the alligator and the teeth cleaning fish or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Right. So, you know, I always wonder why the alligator doesn't just eat the fish, but I guess they're brushing its teeth basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So Ethereum is it gives you more transactional flexibility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's much more experimentation happening there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It has this whole decentralized finance element.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's a huge number of bitcoins that circulate on the Ethereum protocol.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Right. Because Ethereum is open to other asset types basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I think that's actually a creative to both systems because Ethereum gets to have this good form of collateral Bitcoin on the system, which is good volatility characteristics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And then it's a supply sink for bitcoins, which are sort of now they're injected into this third party protocol.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that, I think, reduces the velocity of Bitcoin over on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's probably good for the valuation. So you see it's quite possibly could be a symbiotic relationship.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's really interesting. I think so. I think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: What are your thoughts about Vitalik Buterin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: What are your thoughts about some of the other figures in the space outside of Bitcoin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think Vitalik made some mistakes with Ethereum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Ultimately, like I disagree with some of the decisions that were made along the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Like there's this infamous case of this bailout where 14 percent of ether was lost in the smart contract.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Or really the this smart contract that a lot of Ethereum leadership were sort of backing and supporting was hacked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And then the foundation with Vitalik support chose to make a change to the underlying protocol to undo the hack.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Right. So to me, that was not the most prudent approach because you're basically violating the core protocol rules in order to undo, you know, to bail out a specific contract, which has failed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Granted, there was a lot of ether in there, but I think that shook the credibility of the Ethereum system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It happened back in 2016, I think. That was one reason why I became disenchanted with Ethereum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So basically, even if in that case that might fix an important problem that opens the door to centralized like manipulation of the protocol in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, it basically demonstrates that there's certain elites at the protocol level that can exercise specific control over the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And, you know, a lot of people have lost money and hacks on Ethereum and a lot of contracts have gone south.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Huge amount of value, but they didn't get a bailout.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And it was just when, you know, this specific contract called the DAO was hacked that, you know, the leadership intervened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And, you know, to their credit, they haven't had a significant intervention or bailout since then, but it did normalize the practice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And I think it weakened the social contract.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I would prefer that you sort of bite the bullet in that situation and you accept the failure of that contract.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That would be a ballsy move to bite that bullet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah. I mean, and then you would have had like what they thought was a malicious entity and control of a lot of coins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think the real reason they sort of felt that they had to undo it was because they'd always planned to move to this proof of stake world

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: where your political control over the system is a function of your wealth in the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And they didn't want this attacker, which would have inherited all this significant wealth, to have influence over that future proof of stake version.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's sort of my theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah. I mean, that makes sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It kind of reminds me of the bailout of car companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You know, this is difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's a lot of people that criticize the bailout of these large companies, you know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Creative destruction. I mean, I was critical of the bailouts that happened during COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, I generally think that it's healthier for society for bad firms that are making money to fail or be reorganized under the various forms of bankruptcy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And you saw what happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You see the corporate sector in Japan in the 90s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's this like slow motion insolvency where basically firms weren't allowed to fail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And the Japanese corporate sector lost competitiveness because bad firms did not fail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so, you know, the process of actual capitalism for the market clearing didn't occur.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I'm always in support of, you know, of the free market being allowed to clear for non-profitable firms to fail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's complicated, man, because creative destruction seems to be in the long term a positive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But human civilization is such that short-term pain has real impact on people, you know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, policymakers don't ever want to incur that short-term pain because they have a short-term outlook and term limits often.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But and also just it's short-term pain. Forget policymakers, forget politicians.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It sucks to lose a job for an individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You know, you could say the company, you know, creative destruction of a company means the company was inefficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that's going to have a ripple effect of teaching everybody else what an efficient operation looks like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But like there's jobs that are being lost. There's families that have to suffer because of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, that's the tension we live in society is having a basic safety net for our world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Because there's a level beyond which, like if through creative destruction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: you have some percent of the population that dips below a certain level that you would call like suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: We don't want that. And that's a difficult thing to live with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yes, in the long term, you want inefficiency to be destroyed and efficiency to be rewarded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But there does seem to be a base level of like quality of life that we want to uphold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's a difficult thing to think about. I think about that a lot. There's a doctor called Paul Farmer that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: you know, there's like in Haiti or in Africa, there's a child who's dying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And as a doctor, you want to give everything you have, all the money you have to save that one child.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But there, you know, and you do actually. But that's a very human action.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's not an economic, it's not a rational action from a game theoretic perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: because there's no way you can take that action for every child who is suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But there's something deeply human about doing that for that one particular child.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And in that same sense, creative destruction is an economic principle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But it's not necessarily that same kind of human principle. And there's a tension there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I see it. I mean, I think that's the issue with modern central banking really,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: is that the central bank always has an incentive to lower interest rates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And they've been doing that from the 70s towards today on this, you know, well, 80s, really on this slow march down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Because whenever there was a hint of a crisis in the economy or financial asset prices started to fall,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: their reaction is, okay, well, inject more capital into the economy. We'll save it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But my view is that these plaited short term measures cause the buildup of a huge amount of fragility in the long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And then the ultimate collapse is much worse than the counterfactual situation where you raised interest rates,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: you took your medicine, and the economy was healthier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So and that's sort of that's why people like Ray Dalio point out that you have these long term debt cycles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And we're sort of at the end of one now is because we couldn't take our medicine. We couldn't, you know, let interest rates clear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: We constantly wanted to ward off any difficulty. And we didn't ever want to deleverage truly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And then when the when the debt crisis happens and it hits, it's, you know, horrendously bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So do you think Bitcoin might reach a million dollars in value?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's it's having a current resurgence, a crazy one in 2021 in the recent months of over 60,000, I guess it is now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Do you think it's possible it goes over 100,000? Do you think it's possible goes to a million?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You can't rule anything out with Bitcoin. So I mean, I'm not, you know, one to put price targets on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But one way it could reach a million dollars is Bitcoin's value stays unchanged in real terms and dollar precious dollar depreciates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's not that I expect hyperinflation. But yeah, I mean, like Bitcoin is worth about one tenth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: slightly under one tenth the value of all the gold in the world. And, you know, gold is worth 10 trillion, 11 trillion dollars in the aggregate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Do I think Bitcoin can be more culturally and economically salient than gold in two decades time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: 100 percent. Bitcoin was unknown 12 years ago and today 100 million people worldwide own Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So just extrapolate that. What is the level of penetration you think we'll get? 500 million, a billion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You know, you can easily tune these adoption curves however you like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I don't think it's done, you know, monetizing and being adopted globally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Do you think it can become like the base layer for a lot of our financial operation, like it become the main base layer for all our transactions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So like even even banks will use Bitcoin essentially and like Visa would use Bitcoin as the base layer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Like it would actually operate very similarly at the at the surface layer, but at the base layer would all be Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's precisely what I expect. And banks and Visa are already using Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So Visa has embraced Bitcoin in a really big way, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And it's always funny to the people saying Bitcoin has to change in a certain way so it can compete with Visa.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: No, Visa adopted Bitcoin, right? PayPal adopted Bitcoin, Square adopted Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Obviously, they're not tearing out all of their existing infrastructure, but they're totally engaging with this thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Banks have now begun. They got the green light to provide custody for Bitcoin for their depositors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's the first step. Eventually, you know, it'll happen one of two ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Either Bitcoin native financial institutions will become banks. That's already happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's Bitcoin exchanges that have gotten banking licenses or banks themselves will start to engage with Bitcoin as a reserve asset.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It'll converge either way. That's totally happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And yes, I mean, I don't think Bitcoin is going to power every financial transaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think it will coexist alongside sovereign currencies. But I think it's a great reserve asset.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's a very powerful asset to build a financial system on top of because it's highly, highly auditable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's something that you can take physical delivery of very cheaply. And those are great qualities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: If you're a depositor in a bank, they can prove to you how much Bitcoin they have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: They can't really easily prove, you know, in the old system, how much gold they held on deposit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And you can easily conduct a run on the bank. You can hold them accountable because you can withdraw it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Because, you know, making a Bitcoin transaction is pretty easy at the end of the day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Unlike fiat currency, it's like kind of you can't really withdraw all your dollars from the bank.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, you sort of can, but you're not going to want to take delivery of pounds of cash or anything like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So it's a good modern asset upon which to build a financial system, basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You mentioned Square and Visa sort of investing in Bitcoin. What do you make of probably one of the higher profile big investments in Bitcoin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: which is Tesla and Elon Musk, but there's also a few billionaires like Chamath and all of them investing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: What do you make of this whole movement? Why do you think they're doing it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, Tesla is an interesting case. Why do you think Tesla is putting buying so much Bitcoin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I honestly don't know. And I would love to truly know Elon's genuine thoughts on Bitcoin because he's kind of sending us mixed messages, honestly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: with his embrace of Dogecoin, which is sort of playful. Not exactly sure what point he's trying to make there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So you were involved with Dogecoin. You mentioned offline a little bit in like in the early days, or at least like played around with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: What do you make of Dogecoin? What do you make of Elon and Doge? What do you make of this particular meme coin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Is it one, like a legitimate cryptocurrency, or is it two, like a funny internet way of saying F you to the man?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, it's a good question. I mean, so I wasn't like a figurehead in Dogecoin or anything, but that was totally my introduction to crypto was mining Dogecoin in my dorm room

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and then tipping people online in Dogecoin, which I just thought was the funniest thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I guess I was really easy to entertain back in 2013. But it was very playful at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There was a culture around Dogecoin and the people liked it because it was in opposition to the Bitcoin culture,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Speaking of which, you've written a little bit about NFTs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173
