body.input: What do you think of NFTs?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, I think the current enthusiasm for NFTs and the financial metrics you see the growth there in that sector is partially a function of where we are in the actual credit cycle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So oftentimes when inflationary events occur, you have correspondence speculative manias that occur at the same time because people intuitively feel that the fiat currency that they hold is being debased.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so they frantically look around for other places to put it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So stocks, property, commodities, and then other asset classes, NFTs are an asset class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And this is a case with any inflation you look at in history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You saw these correspond speculative manias, basically speculative episodes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So a lot of us feel that inflation is occurring, whether it's in the CPI or not, that basically lots of dollars are being injected into the economy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: We have all seen stocks massively appreciate even as GDP contracted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so a lot of people sort of got caught on to this notion that, wow, is the Fed lowers interest rates and Congress spends a huge amount of stimulus dollars into the economy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Financial assets going to go up. So I better have exposure to all that stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so you see virtually every asset class is awash with cash right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: People are investing like their lives depend on it, investing, trading, whatever, whether it's options, volumes on Robin Hood,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: retail, brokerages, things like that, whether it's stocks, whether it's crypto, and then other collectibles, baseball cards, their valuations have been skyrocketing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so I think NFTs are part of that. It's a new asset class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's basically an opportunity to invest in sort of art or collectibles, in-game items, things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think that explains a large degree of the enthusiasm. The excitement is that it's a novel asset class that people can trade and right as these inflationary tailwinds pick up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Now, as for the sort of virtues of the actual technical phenomenon, NFTs are actually not a new idea at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So you've had NFTs, I didn't call them NFTs, but in 2016 built on Bitcoin, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So it's been around for a while. What it is is a serial code, basically a string of data that is inserted onto a public blockchain and then circulates as a unique token.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And then the question is, okay, well, what does that data refer to? What's the external reference?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that has to be defined. There has to be some entity which says, oh yeah, this unique string refers to like this piece of art or digital content or trading card or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So NFTs, the concept itself is like an incredibly broad idea. It's just, well, what if we took barcodes and put them on chain so that they could be traded

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and so they could circulate freely on a peer-to-peer basis and plugged into exchanges and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So that concept is super valid, clearly has protocol market fit, right? People are using it for a really wide array of purposes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's completely going to exist. May the valuations contract of NFTs in the aggregate? Definitely possible, probably likely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But I think the notion of creating enduring collectibles or artworks that have accompanying signatures, basically autographed art on the blockchain, that has totally been validated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think that won't go away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I wonder if there's ideas like BitCloud, for example. I don't know if you saw that. If there's ideas built on top of this concept, it doesn't have to be like Ethereum, NFTs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It could be just the concept of non-fungible tokens, whether those kinds of things could take hold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So just the financial aspect is a way to put some validity behind the identity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I wonder if there's ideas there that are yet to be discovered or ideas that are yet to take hold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And it's unclear whether it's a scam yet or not. It's unclear where it's coming from.

body.input: There's open questions around it. But are public blockchains and that sort of architecture,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: is that going to be useful for decentralized or alternative forms of social media?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: 100% yes. I'm super, super bullish on that idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Basically, creating open protocols, open namespaces, ways to organize without the dependence on a single node,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: effectively in Silicon Valley, the Twitter node or the Facebook node.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think it's a matter of urgency that we create digital gathering spaces where you have strong property rights.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: the layers of lull, like the layers of not taking anything seriously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And I think there's power to that. There's freedom to that. I appreciate it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I have respect for it, but it's not my thing on Twitter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's just not the way I enjoy communicating on Twitter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I retired from Twitter. I hit 100,000 followers and then I retired.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I'm free now. I don't have to tweet anymore. It's great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But I totally can see the point. I wish that Bitcoiners were gentler in their approach.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Not all Bitcoiners are like that. Of course, there's 50 to 100 million of them worldwide and a few tens of thousands on Twitter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I'm not going to claim that they're necessarily representative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: The toxicity, though, is kind of a learned habit because Bitcoin has had so many episodes where strong-willed institutions, billionaires,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: the dice are pretty toxic, you could say, right? I'm basically mocking critics of Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But at the same time, you're saying that the criticism has been predictable and repeatable and it's been the same throughout.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, and that's a pretty dismissive thing to say, right? That I can reduce you to an algorithm with 11 permutations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But the thing to remember, I guess, is that some of the best-funded companies in the Bitcoin space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: the most powerful miners, billionaires have tried to change and co-opt and alter Bitcoin to shape it to their liking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And without these incredibly hardcore sort of high priests of the Bitcoin protocol, it would have been hopeless, hopelessly maliated in all number of ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so there is a reason why someone would be incredibly protective of Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Does that justify immense toxicity on social media? Probably not. But it's a leaderless protocol.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So the whole point is that it's money for enemies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And some of the Bitcoin maximalists came for me, too, when I made suggestions that they didn't like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But I'm happy to use the protocol because I know that that transaction will be final,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: regardless of how odious my counterparty is or how politically disfavored their opinions are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: See, I mean, and this is where there could be disagreements, but I think you have to think about what's effective as a defense mechanism of strong ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And I personally think that kindness and thoughtfulness is much more effective because it lets the idea shine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: as opposed to the personality of the individual humans overriding it. But there's debates on this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, I take your side on that. I think a patient and careful approach is the way to go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Now, do all critics deserve good faith engagement? No, I would say a lot of critics of Bitcoin operate in extreme bad faith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And the reason why is because we're not just talking about technical questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: In fact, most of this conversation has not been technical. It's been political because Bitcoin is an intensely political idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so a lot of people are predisposed to totally hate it and to wish death on Bitcoiners.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, there was a professor at GW I saw earlier this week that was musing about getting all the Bitcoiners on a boat and sinking it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: In what other context would a upstanding professor muse about mass murder? But in the context of Bitcoin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: it's sort of OK within his peers because you're talking about something that most people don't like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's a concept that's alien to them, that doesn't jive with the way they see the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so because it's so pitched from a political perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: there's a lot of critics as well as defenders that operate in bad faith, I would say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But that's the nature of the beast. It's because we're proposing a very disruptive thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And there are people that would be disrupted by it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You wrote a blog post titled On Writing. You're, I think, an excellent writer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So let me ask, what does it take to be a good writer? What does it take to write some of the blog posts you've written?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Sort of condensed set of ideas in your head, the mess that's probably in your head and putting down on paper

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: in a way that communicates the idea clearly and powerfully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So that was basically the point of the blog post is that being an impressive writer is different from being an effective writer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I think the answer to your question is humility, basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So I think if you let pride and vanity seep into your writing, then you risk creating a very noisy signal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: creating a very inefficient channel for communicating literal neural arrangements from your brain to someone else's brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that's what I think about when I write is like, wow, I have the power to at scale change the literal physical composition of people's brains, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: To rewire them. If I make an idea that's so persuasive, that's so sticky, if I coin a phrase that is so pithy, then I can alter their brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's crazy. I mean, you're letting someone reach into your head and mess with it a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's unbelievable. And that's like a superpower. And if you could do that to 100,000 people at once, how powerful is that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You mentioned Descartes, I think therefore I am. That's like literally rewired millions of brains throughout history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Right. I mean, that's one of the most powerful, like Cogito Urgo Sum, one of the most powerful phrases ever written.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that sent a zillion philosophy undergraduates down a rabbit hole of skepticism that some of them didn't make it out of, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: and they're convinced that, you know, the brain in the vat theory is true and there's no way to know, you know, what are our tangible experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But yeah, so that's the beauty of writing. And the thing that interferes with that is our pride, our desire to, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: impress people and, you know, look good to them and show off our vocab and stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that's that was the point of that piece is that I went on this journey where I eventually realized that I don't know if I'm any better of a writer for having realized it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But I think that is a necessary condition. So does that mean there is a value to striving for simplicity in the words as opposed to?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, complexity. I think so for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And we deal with complex topics all the time and crypto. And that's always a huge red flag for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, if you can't explain something simply, do you understand it? You know, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So if you're talking about something that complex, if you can't find simple ways to discuss it, my presumption is that you're actually obfuscating the truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And this is what Orwell railed against with political language. You know, he really hated political language because he felt that its authors were using deliberate obfuscation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And, you know, he hated euphemisms and I hate euphemisms, too. You know, I much prefer, you know, forthrightness and clarity of thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But most people when they write don't really endeavor to be particularly clear. They might be writing to show off their startup or, you know, to demonstrate to people how cool they are or how well read they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You know, they're displaying it's like a peacock style display. What fraction of people write to actually communicate meaning small fraction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's especially difficult because what I've detected is something in us humans as readers assigned more credibility to people that obfuscate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So, like, simple, clear communication of an idea is not like the immediate reaction is not one where we assign credibility to the person like like that was that was brilliant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's a lot of people that I kind of listen to without really understanding what the heck they're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And but it sounds musical and smart. And then I see a lot of folks assigning credibility to that person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And it's unfortunate. It's unfortunate that there's that tension as a reader that we appreciate the beauty and power of like complex weaving of words without assigning as much value to like actual clear communication of an idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And I'm always skeptical in speech as well. When someone will describe someone as articulate, I'm always immediately skeptical of the value of what that person is saying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Because if you articulate, you can make bad ideas sound very acceptable and great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Noam Chomsky has said this before. He has a way to defend the way he speaks. He said that like he's suspicious of charismatic people because they can basically sell any kind of idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: He speaks in a very monotone and boring way so that whatever the value his ideas have, they'll shine through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's something to that. There's something to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But it's a difficult journey. It's a difficult path because then I think it's the right path because ultimately you focus on the quality of your ideas. And in the long term, that wins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I agree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Just by way of advice, is there if people are interested in Bitcoin or cryptocurrency in your work, what are good books or resources on Bitcoin from you and from others that you can recommend that were in your own journey helped you or you've seen help others?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Well, it's very easy. It's much easier today to make the Bitcoin journey because the quality of content is so much better than it was when I started.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, when I learned about Bitcoin, there was the Bitcoin Wiki and the Bitcoin Stack Exchange and the subreddit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And that was kind of it. And you had to just pick up everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: The economic theory hadn't really been worked out very much. So you had to pick everything up from scratch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: The good news is that there's a huge abundance of content. And that's actually one of Bitcoin's greatest strengths is that people are totally inspired to write about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And it's almost a rite of passage at this point. If you're like a Bitcoin thinker to have your book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I don't have a book yet. I would love to recommend my book. I haven't written one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Do you think about writing a book?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Yeah, I think it's my duty. 100%.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Everyone that has created a lot of Bitcoin content probably should condense it into a book to give it an enduring status.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's interesting because you mentioned block size wars and you've written on a lot of different topics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So you could both write like a big like Sapien style book about Bitcoin or cryptocurrency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But you can also write a book on each like a specific thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And now that you put pressure on yourself and talk and talk about simplicity, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Where do you lean on those different book journeys that you might take on?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Do you have in you eventually like a like a Bitcoin book?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, I tallied up the words that I wrote in the last couple of years on Bitcoin. It's like over 100,000 words a year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So that's two novels there. But yeah, I think I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I think there's so much underexplored space in Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, a systematic interpretation of Satoshi's writings, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And a lot of people don't want anyone to do that because they don't want it to have these religious overtones where you're engaging in interpretation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You know, but that's something that should be done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There's a lot of Bitcoin histories that haven't been written.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: There was a great Bitcoin history recently published.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: That's this is one of my recommendations is on the block size war by Jonathan Beer, who runs probably the best research desk in the industry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So there's huge amounts of history that has transpired that hasn't been chronicled.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And some of the accounts are indifferent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You know, they're often written by outsiders, you know, journalists that maybe don't fully engage with the Bitcoin system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But do you think the humans are interesting in this story, too?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Of course, they're the most interesting thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You know, I mean, Bitcoin itself doesn't really change that much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It's kind of this cold, you know, protocol that just sort of takes along.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But the characters are just fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, and there's so many unbelievable characters in the Bitcoin story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Unbelievable. Yeah, that's the cool thing about Bitcoin and cryptocurrency and just Internet is like the weirdos, the brilliant weirdos.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Like all the people in in the stuff that's already established are boring, like economics professors are all boring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But the interesting people, the wild ones are are the ones that are innovating on in the crypto space, which is, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: that's where the dangerous weirdos are and the exciting, brilliant weirdos.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Well, you have to be kind of crazy to adopt Bitcoin in the first sort of five years of its life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So there is an adverse selection element there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I don't know if that's an uncharitable way to put it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But like some of Bitcoin's earliest evangelists are not the evangelists I would have chosen, but they were the ones that we got.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So it's the one we got. But is there is there resources?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: You're basically saying just throw a dart and most books are going to be good or is there something that's out to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: I mean, your average book is terrible for sure, but not on Bitcoin specifically, but just in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: It depends whether you like the computer science, the economics or the history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But my recommendations would be, you know, obviously the Bitcoin white paper that's and Satoshi's complementary writings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: See, the problem with advice is that in a world where so much of success is defined by luck and serendipity is that the advice givers often don't know why they've been successful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Right. And so they might say, you know, I was wearing a green tie on the day of my job interview.

body.input: And so you should go out and wear green ties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And so they might just get the causality completely wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Right. I mean, I'm not going to claim that I'm super successful yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But see, that's the problem is that I don't think my journey is replicable necessarily.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: So, you know, who am I to give advice?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Although the one thing I will say is that the thing I did right was to become completely obsessed with a domain I found really interesting and held promise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: Like if I had been really interested in like Magic the Gathering, I wouldn't have been able to like do much with that aside from build like a killer card pack or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: And I wasn't afraid to, you know, really put myself out there and, you know, float my thoughts online and see how people reacted to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

metadata.title: Podcast: Nic Carter: Bitcoin Core Values, Layered Scaling, and Blocksize Debates | Lex Fridman Podcast #173

body.input: But you do have to make yourself available to it. And you have to take a ton of chances.

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Brian Kernigan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Unix started being developed 50 years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It'd be more than 50 years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Can you tell the story like you describe in your new book of how Unix was created?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Huh?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: If I can remember that far back, it was some while ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So I think the gist of it is that at Bell Labs in 1969, there were a group of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: who had just finished working on the Multics project, which was itself a

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: follow on to CTSS.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So we can go back sort of an infinite regress in time, but the CTSS was a very,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: very, very nice time sharing system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was very nice to use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I actually used it as that summer I spent in Cambridge in 1966.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What was the hardware there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So what's the operating system, what's the hardware there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What's the CTS look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So CTSS looked like kind of like a standard time sharing system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Certainly at the time it was the only time sharing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Let's go back to the basic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What's the time sharing system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: In the beginning was the word and the word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And then there was time sharing systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: If we go back into, let's call it the 1950s and early 1960s, most computing was

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: done on very big computers, physically big, although not terribly powerful by

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: today's standards that were maintained in very large rooms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And you use things like punch cards to write your programs on, talk to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So you would take a deck of cards, write your program on it, send it over a

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: counter, hand it to an operator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And some while later back would come something that said, oh, you made a

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: mistake and then you'd recycle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so it was very, very slow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So the idea of time sharing was that you take basically that same computer, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: connect to it with something that looked like an electric typewriter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: They could be a long distance away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It could be close, but fundamentally what the operating system did was to give

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: each person who was connected to it and wanting to do something, a small slice

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: of time on, to do a particular job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So I might be editing a file.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So I would be typing and every time I hit a keystroke, the operating system would

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: wake up and said, oh, he typed character.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Let me remember that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Then it'd go back to doing something else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So it'd be going around and around a group of people who were trying to get

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: something done, giving each a small slice of time and giving them each the illusion

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: that they pretty much had the whole machine to themselves, enhance time sharing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That is sharing the computing time resource of the computer among a

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: number of people who are doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Without the individual people being aware that there's others in a sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: the illusion, the feelings that you have, the machine is, you know, you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: doing it, you're doing it, you're doing it, you're doing it, you're doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So it's a whole machine to yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it was very much better than the punch card model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so CTSS, the compatible time sharing system was, I think, arguably the first

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: of these, it was done, I guess, technically in 64 or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It ran on an IBM 7094, slightly modified to have twice the speed of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: machine, but it was a very good machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Like that it ran on an IBM 7094, slightly modified to have twice as much memory

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: as the norm, it had two banks of 32K words instead of one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So 32K words, each word was 36 bits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So call it, you know, about 150 kilobytes times two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So by today's standards, that's down in the noise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But at the time that was a lot of memory and memory was expensive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So CTSS was just a wonderful environment to work on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was done by the people at MIT, led by Fernando Corbato, Corby, who died

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: just earlier this year, and a bunch of other folks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And then, so I spent the summer of 66 working on that, had a great time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: met a lot of really nice people and indirectly knew of people at Bell Labs

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: who were also working on a follow-on to CTSS that was called Multics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So Multics was meant to be the system that would do everything that CTSS

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: did, but do it better for a larger population, all the usual stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Now the actual time sharing, the scheduling, how much, what's the algorithm

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: that performs the scheduling?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What's that look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: How much magic is there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What are the metrics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: How does it all work in the beginning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So the answer is I don't have a clue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think the basic idea was nothing more than who all wants to get something done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Suppose that things are very quiet in the middle of the night, then I get

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: all the time that I want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Suppose that you and I are contending at high noon for something like that, then

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: probably the simplest algorithm is a round robin one that gives you a bit of time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: gives me a bit of time, and then we could adapt to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Like, what are you trying to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Are you text editing or are you compiling or something?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And then we might adjust the scheduler according to things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So, okay. So Multics was trying to just do some of the, clean it up a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Well, it was meant to be much more than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So Multics was the multiplexed information and computing service, and it was meant to

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: be a very large thing that would provide computing utility, something that where

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: you could actually think of it as just a plug in the wall service, sort of like

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: cloud computing today, same idea, but 50 odd years earlier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Forgive me if it's a dumb question, but it feels like a daunting task to write any kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: of complex system in assembly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It feels like impossible to do any kind of what we think of as software engineering with

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: assembly, to work on a big picture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think it's hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's been a long time since I wrote assembly language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It is absolutely true that in assembly language, if you make a mistake, nobody tells you there

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: are no terms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Absolutely true that in assembly language, if you make a mistake, nobody tells you there

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: are no training wheels whatsoever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So stuff doesn't work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Now what?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: There's no debuggers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Well, there could be debuggers, but that's the same problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: How do you actually get something that will help you debug it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Part of it is an ability to see the big picture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Now, these systems were not big in the sense that today's pictures are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So the big picture was in some sense more manageable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I mean, then realistically, there's an enormous variation in the capabilities of programmers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And Ken Thompson, who did that first one, is kind of the singularity in my experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: of programmers with no disrespect to you or even to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: He's in several leagues removed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I know there's levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's a fascinating thing that there are unique stars in particular in the programming space

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: and in a particular time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: The time matters, too, the timing of when that person comes along.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And a wife does have to leave.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: There's this weird timing that happens and then all of a sudden something beautiful is

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: created.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I mean, how does it make you feel that there's a system that was created in three weeks or

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: maybe you can even say on a whim, but not really, but of course quickly, that is now

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: you could think of most of the computers in the world run on a Unix-like system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: How do you like, if you kind of zoom from the alien perspective, if you were just observing

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Earth, that all of a sudden these computers took over the world and they started from

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: this little initial seed of Unix, how does that make you feel?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's quite surprising.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And you asked earlier about prediction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: The answer is no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: There's no way you could predict that kind of evolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And I don't know whether it was inevitable or just a whole sequence of blind luck, I

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: suspect more of the latter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so I look at it and think, gee, that's kind of neat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think the real question is what does Ken think about that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Because he's the guy arguably from whom it really came.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Tremendous contributions from Dennis Ritchie and then others around in that Bell Labs environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But if you had to pick a single person, that would be Ken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So you've written a new book, Unix, a History and a Memoir.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Are there some memorable human stories, funny or profound from that time, that just kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: of stand out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Oh, there's a lot of them in a sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And again, it's a question of can you resurrect them in real time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Memory fails.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But I think part of it was that Bell Labs at the time was a very special kind of place

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: to work because there were a lot of interesting people and the environment was very, very

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: open and free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was a very cooperative environment, very friendly environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so if you had an interesting problem, you go and talk to somebody and they might

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: help you with the solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it was kind of a fun environment too in which people did strange things and often

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: tweaking the bureaucracy in one way or another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So rebellious in certain kinds of ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: In some ways, yeah, absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think most people didn't take too kindly to the bureaucracy and I'm sure the bureaucracy

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: put up with an enormous amount that they didn't really want to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So maybe to linger on it a little bit, do you have a sense of what the philosophy that

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: characterizes Unix is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: The design, not just the initial, but just carry through the years, just being there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: being around it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What's the fundamental philosophy behind the system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think one aspect, the fundamental philosophy was to provide an environment that made it

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: easy to write or easier, productive to write programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So it was meant as a programmer environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It wasn't meant specifically as something to do some other kind of job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: For example, it was used extensively for word processing, but it wasn't designed as a word

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: processing system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was used extensively for lab control, but it wasn't designed for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was used extensively as a front end for big other systems, big dump systems, but it

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: wasn't designed for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was meant to be an environment where it was really easy to write programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So the programmers could be highly productive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And part of that was to be a community, and there's some observation from Dennis Ritchie,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think at the end of the book, it says that from his standpoint, the real goal was to

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: create a community where people could work as programmers on the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think in that sense, certainly for many, many years, it succeeded quite well at that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And part of that is the technical aspects of because it made it really easy to write

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: programs, people did write interesting programs, those programs tended to be used by other

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: programmers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so it was kind of a virtuous circle of more and more stuff coming out that was really

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: good for programmers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And you were part of that community of programmers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So what was it like writing programs on that early Unix?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was a blast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It really was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You know, I like to program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I'm not a terribly good programmer, but it was a lot of fun to write code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And in the early days, there was an enormous amount of what you would today, I suppose,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: call low hanging fruit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: People hadn't done things before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And this was this new environment and the whole combination of nice tools and very responsive

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: system and tremendous colleagues made it possible to write code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You could have an idea in the morning, you could do an experiment with it, you could

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: have something limping along that night or the next day and people would react to it

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: and they would say, oh, that's wonderful, but you're really screwed up here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And the feedback loop was then very, very short and tight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so a lot of things got developed fairly quickly that in many cases still exist today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And I think that was part of what made it fun because programming itself is fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's puzzle solving in a variety of ways, but I think it's even more fun when you do

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: something that somebody else then uses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Even if they whine about it not working, the fact that they used it is part of the reward

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: mechanism.
