metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And what was the method of interaction, the communication, that feedback loop?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I mean, this is before the internet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Certainly before the internet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was mostly physical right there, somebody would come into your office and say something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So these places are all close by, like offices are nearby, so you're really lively into interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Bell Labs was fundamentally one giant building and most of the people were involved in this

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: unique stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: We're in two or three quarters and there was a room, oh, how big was it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Probably call it 50 feet by 50 feet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Make up a number of that, which had some access to computers there as well as in offices and

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: people hung out there and it had a coffee machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so it was mostly very physical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: We did use email, of course, but it was fundamentally for a long time all on one machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So there was no need for internet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's fascinating to think about what computing would be today without Bell Labs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It seems so many people being in the vicinity of each other, sort of getting that quick

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: feedback, working together, so many brilliant people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I don't know where else that could have existed in the world given how that came together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah, well, how does that make you feel that little element of history?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Well, I think that's very nice, but in a sense, it's survivor bias and if it hadn't happened

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: at Bell Labs, there were other places that were doing really interesting work as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Xerox PARC is perhaps the most obvious one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Xerox PARC contributed enormous amount of good material and many of the things we take

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: for granted today in the same way came from Xerox PARC experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I don't think they capitalized in the long run as much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Their parent company was perhaps not as lucky in capitalizing on this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Who knows?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But that's certainly another place where there was a tremendous amount of influence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: There were a lot of good university activities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: MIT was obviously no slouch in this kind of thing and others as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So Unix turned out to be open source because of the various ways that AT&T operated and

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: sort of had to... The focus was on telephones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think that's a mischaracterization in a sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It absolutely was not open source.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was very definitely proprietary, licensed, but it was licensed freely to universities

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: in source code form for many years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Because of that, generations of university students and their faculty people grew up

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: knowing about Unix and there was enough expertise in the community that it then became possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: for people to kind of go off in their own direction and build something that looked

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Unix-like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: The Berkeley version of Unix started with that licensed code and gradually picked up

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: enough of its own code contributions, notably from people like Bill Joy, that eventually

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: it was able to become completely free of any AT&T code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Now there was an enormous amount of legal jockeying around this in the late... early

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: to late 80s, early 90s, something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And then I guess the open source movement might have started when Richard Stallman started

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: to think about this in the late 80s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: By 1991, when Torvalds decided he was going to do a Unix-like operating system, there

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: was enough expertise in the community that first he had a target.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: He could see what to do because the kind of the Unix system call interface and the tools

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: and so on were there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so he was able to build an operating system that at this point, when you say Unix, in

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: many cases what you're really thinking is Linux.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Linux, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's funny that from my distant perception, I felt that Unix was open source without actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: knowing it, but what you're really saying, it was just freely licensed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was freely licensed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So it felt open source in a sense... because universities are not trying to make money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: so it felt open source in a sense that you can get access if you wanted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And a very, very, very large number of universities had the license and they were able to talk

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: to all the other universities who had the license.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so technically not open, technically belonging to AT&T, pragmatically pretty open.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so there's a ripple effect that all the faculty and the students then all grew up

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: and then they went throughout the world and permeated in that kind of way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So what kind of features do you think make for a good operating system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: If you take the lessons of Unix, you said make it easy for programmers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That seems to be an important one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But also Unix turned out to be exceptionally robust and efficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So is that an accident when you focus on the programmer or is that a natural outcome?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think part of the reason for efficiency was that it began on extremely modest hardware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Very, very, very tiny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so you couldn't get carried away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You couldn't do a lot of complicated things because you just didn't have the resources,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: either processor speed or memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so that enforced a certain minimality of mechanisms and maybe a search for generalizations

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: so that you would find one mechanism that served for a lot of different things rather

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: than having lots of different special cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think the file system in Unix is a good example of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: The file system interface in its fundamental form is extremely straightforward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And that means that you can write code very, very effectively for the file system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And then one of those generalizations is that, gee, that file system interface works for

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: all kinds of other things as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so in particular, the idea of reading and writing to devices is the same as reading

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: and writing to a disk that has a file system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And then that gets carried further in other parts of the world, processes become in effect

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: files in a file system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And the Plan 9 operating system, which came along, I guess, in the late 80s or something

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: like that, took a lot of those ideas from the original Unix and tried to push the generalization

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: even further so that in Plan 9, a lot of different resources are file systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: They all share that interface.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So that would be one example where finding the right model of how to do something means

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: that an awful lot of things become simpler.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it means therefore that more people can do useful, interesting things with them without

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: them to think as hard about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So you said you're not a very good programmer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: True.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You're the world's most modest human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Okay, but you'll continue saying that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I understand how this works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But you do radiate a sort of love for programming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So let me ask, do you think programming is more an art or a science?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Is it creativity or kind of rigor?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think it's some of each.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's some combination.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Some of the art is figuring out what it is that you really want to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What should that program be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What would make a good program?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And that's some understanding of what the task is, what the people who might use this

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: program want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And I think that's art in many respects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: The science part is trying to figure out how to do it well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And some of that is real computer science-y stuff, like what algorithm should we use at

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: some point?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Mostly in the sense of being careful to use algorithms that will actually work properly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: scale properly, avoiding quadratic algorithms when a linear algorithm should be the right

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That kind of more formal view of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Same thing for data structures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But also it's, I think, an engineering field as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And engineering is not quite the same as science because engineering, you're working with constraints.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You have to figure out not only what is a good algorithm for this kind of thing, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: what's the most appropriate algorithm given the amount of time we have to compute, the

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: amount of time we have to program, what's likely to happen in the future with maintenance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: who's going to pick this up in the future?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: All of those kind of things that if you're an engineer you get to worry about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Whereas if you think of yourself as a scientist, well, you can maybe push them over the horizon

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: in a way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And if you're an artist, what's that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So just on your own personal level, what's your process like of writing a program?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Say a small and large sort of tinkering with stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Do you just start coding right away and just kind of evolve iteratively with a loose notion

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: or do you plan on a sheet of paper first and then kind of design what they teach you in

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: the kind of software engineering courses in undergrad or something like that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What's your process like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's certainly much more the informal incremental.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: First, I don't write big programs at this point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's been a long time since I wrote a program that was more than, I call it a few hundred

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: or more lines, something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Many of the programs I write are experiments for either something I'm curious about or

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: often for something that I want to talk about in a class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so those necessarily tend to be relatively small.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: A lot of the kind of code I write these days tends to be for sort of exploratory data analysis

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: where I've got some collection of data and I want to try and figure out what on earth

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: is going on in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And for that, those programs tend to be very small.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Sometimes you're not even programming, you're just using existing tools like counting things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Or sometimes you're writing OCK scripts because two or three lines will tell you something

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: about a piece of data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And then when it gets bigger, well, then I will probably write something in Python because

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: that scales better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Up to call it a few hundred lines or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it's been a long time since I wrote programs that were much more than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Speaking of data exploration and OCK, first, what is OCK?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So OCK is a scripting language that was done by myself, Al Ajo and Peter Weinberger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: We did that originally in the late 70s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It was a language that was meant to make it really easy to do quick and dirty tasks like

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: counting things or selecting interesting information from basically all text files, rearranging

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: it in some way or summarizing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Runs a command on each line of a file.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it's still exceptionally widely used today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Oh, absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's so simple and elegant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: The way to explore data turns out you can just write a script that does something seemingly

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: trivial in a single line and that giving you that slice of the data somehow reveals something

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: fundamental about the data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And that seems to work still.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's very good for that kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That's sort of what it was meant for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think what we didn't appreciate was that the model was actually quite good for a lot

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: of data processing kinds of tasks and that it's kept going as long as it has because

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: at this point it's over 40 years old and it's still, I think, a useful tool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Well, this is paternal interest, I guess, but I think in terms of programming languages,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: you get the most bang for the buck by learning OCK.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It doesn't scale the big programs, but it does pretty darn well on these little things

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: where you just want to see all the somethings in something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So, yeah, I find I probably write more OCK than anything else at this point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So what kind of stuff do you love about OCK?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: If you can comment on sort of things that give you joy when you can in a simple program

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: reveal something about the data, is there something that stands out from particular

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: features?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think it's mostly the selection of default behaviors that you sort of hinted at a moment

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What OCK does is to read through a set of files and then within each file it reads through

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: each of the lines and then on each of the lines it has a set of patterns that it looks

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: for, that's your OCK program, and if one of the patterns matches there is a corresponding

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: action that you might perform.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so it's kind of a quadruply nested loop or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And that's all completely automatic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You don't have to say anything about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You just write the pattern and the action and then run the data by it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so that paradigm for programming is a very natural and effective one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And I think we captured that reasonably well in OCK and it does other things for free as

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It splits the data into fields so that on each line there is fields separated by whitespace

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so it does that for free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You don't have to say anything about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it collects information as it goes along, like what line are we on?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: How many fields are there on this line?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So lots of things that just make it so that a program which in another language, let's

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: say Python, would be 5, 10, 20 lines in OCK is one or two lines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So because it's one or two lines you can do it on the shell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You don't have to open up another whole thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You can just do it right there in the interaction with the operative directly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Is there other shell commands that you love over the years that you really enjoy using?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Oh, grep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Grep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Grep is the only one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah, grep does everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So grep is a kind of a, what is it, a simpler version of OCK I would say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: In some sense, yeah, right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What is grep?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So grep is, it basically searches the input for particular patterns, regular expressions

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: technically of a certain class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it has that same paradigm that OCK does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's a pattern action thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It reads through all the files and then all the lines in each file, but it has a single

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: pattern, which is the regular expression you're looking for and a single action printed if

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: it matches.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So in that sense, it's a much simpler version and you could write grep in OCK as a one-liner.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And I use grep probably more than anything else at this point just because it's so convenient

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: and natural.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Why do you think, it's such a powerful tool, grep and OCK.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Why do you think operating systems like Windows, for example, don't have it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Sort of, you can, of course I use the, which is amazing now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: There's Windows for Linux, which you could basically use all the fun stuff like OCK and

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: grep inside of Windows, but Windows naturally sort of as part of the graphical interface,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: the simplicity of grep, sort of searching through a bunch of files and just popping

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: up naturally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Why don't you think that, why do you think that's unique to the Linux environment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's not strictly unique, but it's certainly focused there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And I think some of it's the weight of history that Windows came from MS-DOS.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: MS-DOS was a pretty pathetic operating system, although common on an unboundedly large number

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: of machines, but somewhere in roughly the 90s, Windows became a graphical system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And I think Microsoft spent a lot of their energy on making that graphical interface

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: what it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And that's a different model of computing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's a model of computing that where you point and click and sort of experiment with menus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's a model of computing works rather well for people who are not programmers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: People want to get something done, whereas teaching something like the command line to

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: non-programmers turns out to sometimes be an uphill struggle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so I think Microsoft probably was right in what they did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Now you mentioned Whistle or whatever it's called, the Linux.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Whistle, I wonder what it's pronounced.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: W-S-L is what, I've never actually pronounced the whistle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I like it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I have no idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Whistle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But there have been things like that for a long, SigWin, for example, which is a wonderful

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: collection of take all your favorite tools from Unix and Linux and just make them work

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: perfectly on Windows.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so that's something that's been going on for at least 20 years, if not longer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And I use that on my one remaining Windows machine routinely because if you're doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: something that is batch computing, suitable for command line, that's the right way to

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: do it because the Windows equivalents are, if nothing else, not familiar to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But I would definitely recommend to people to, if they don't use SigWin, to try Whistle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I've been so excited that I could use BASH, write scripts quickly in Windows.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's changed my life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What's your perfect programming setup?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What computer, what operating system, what keyboard, what editor?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Perfect is too strong a word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's way too strong a word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What I use by default, I have at this point a 13 inch MacBook Air, which I use because

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: it's kind of a reasonable balance of the various things I need.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I can carry it around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's got enough computing horse bars, screen's big enough, keyboard's okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so I basically do most of my computing on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I have a big iMac in my office that I use from time to time as well, especially when

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I need a big screen, but otherwise it tends not to be used that much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Editor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I use mostly SAM, which is an editor that Rob Pike wrote long ago at Bell Labs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Sorry to interrupt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Does that proceed VI?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Does that proceed EMAX?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It post dates both VI and EMAX.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It is derived from Rob's experience with ED and VI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That's the original Unix editor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Oh wow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: He said probably before you were born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So what's the history of editors?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Can you briefly, I use EMAX, I'm sorry to say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Sorry to come out with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But what's the kind of interplay there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So in ancient times, call it the first time sharing systems going back to what we were

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: There was an editor on CTSS that I don't even remember what it was called.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So it might've been edit where you could type text, program text, and it would do something

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: or document text.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You could save the text.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And save it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You could edit it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You know, the usual thing that you would get in an editor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And Ken Thompson wrote an editor called QED, which was very, very powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But these were all totally a command-based.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: They were not most or cursor-based because it was before mice and even before cursors

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: because they were running on terminals that printed on paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: No CRT type displays, let alone LEDs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so then when UNIX came along, Ken took QED and stripped it way, way, way, way down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And that became an editor that he called ED.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it was very simple, but it was a line-oriented editor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so you could load a file and then you could talk about the lines one through the

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: last line and you could, you know, print ranges of lines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You could add text.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You could delete text.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You could change text.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Or you could do a substitute command that would change things within a line or within

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: groups of lines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So you can work on a parts of a file essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You could work on any part of it, the whole thing or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But it was entirely command line-based and it was entirely on paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And that meant that you changed it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Actual paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah, right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Real paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so if you changed the line, you had to print that line using up another line of paper

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: to see what the change caused.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so when CRT displays came along, then you could start to use cursor control and

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: you could sort of move where you were on the screen in...

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Without reprinting every time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Without reprinting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And there were a number of editors there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: The one that I was most familiar with and still use is VI, which was done by Bill Choi.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so that dates from probably the late 70s as a guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it took a full advantage of the cursor controls.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I suspected eMAX was roughly at the same time, but I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I've never internalized eMAX.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So at this point, I stopped using ED, although I still can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I use VI sometimes and I use SAM when I can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And SAM is available on most systems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It is available.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You have to download it yourself from typically the Plan 9 operating system distribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's been maintained by people there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so I...

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I'll get home tonight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I'll try it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It sounds fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Although my love is with Lisp and eMAX, I've went into that hippie world of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think it's a lot of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: What religion were you brought up with?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah, that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Most of the actual programming I do is C, C++, and Python, but my weird sort of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I'm not sure if I'm a little bit of a

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: brainless or a little bit of a brainless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So can you take on the impossible task and give a brief history of programming languages

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: from your perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So I guess you could say programming languages started probably in what, the late 40s or

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: People used to program computers by basically putting in zeros and ones using something

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: like switches on a console and then...

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Or maybe holes in paper tapes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So extremely tedious, awful, whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so I think the first programming languages were relatively crude assembly languages where

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: people would basically write a program that would convert mnemonics like add add into

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: whatever the bit pattern was that corresponded to an add instruction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And they would do the clerical work of figuring out where things were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So you could put a name on a location in a program and the assembler would figure out

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: where that corresponded to when the thing was all put together and dropped into memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And early on, and this would be the late 40s and very early 50s, there were assemblers

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: written for the various machines that people used.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You may have seen in the paper just a couple of days ago, Tony Berker died.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: He did this thing in Manchester called the, called auto code, a language which I knew

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: only by name.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But it sounds like it was a flavor of assembly language, sort of a little higher in some

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it replaced a language that Alan Turing wrote, which you put in zeros and ones, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: you put in backwards order because that was hardware work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Very strange.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It's backwards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So assembly languages, then let's call that the early 1950s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so every different flavor of computer has its own assembly language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So the Ed Sac had its and the Manchester had its and the IBM whatever, 7090 or 704 or whatever

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: had its and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So everybody had their own assembly language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And assembly languages have a few commands, additions, subtraction, then branching of

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: some kind if then type of situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: They have exactly in their simplest form, at least one instruction per or one assembly

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: language instruction per instruction in the machine's repertoire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so you have to know the machine intimately to be able to write programs in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And if you write an assembly language program for one kind of machine and then you say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: geez, it's nice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I'd like a different machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Start over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So very bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so what happened in the late 50s was people realized you could play this game again and

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: you could move up a level in writing or creating languages that were closer to the way that

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: real people might think about how to write code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And there were, I guess, arguably three or four at that time period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: There was Fortran, which came from IBM, which was formula translation meant to make it easy

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: to do scientific and engineering computations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I just know that formula translation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That's what it stood for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: There was COBOL, which is the common business oriented language that Grace Hopper and others

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: worked on, which was aimed at business kinds of tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: There was ALGOL, which was mostly meant to describe algorithmic computations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I guess you could argue BASIC was in there somewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: I think it's just a little later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so all of those moved the level up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so they were closer to what you and I might think of as we were trying to write

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: a program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And they were focused on different domains, Fortran for formula translation, engineering

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: computations, let's say COBOL for business, that kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And still used today, at least Fortran probably.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Oh yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: COBOL too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: But the deal was that once you moved up that level, then you, let's call it Fortran, you

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: had a language that was not tied to a particular kind of hardware because a different compiler

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: would compile for different kinds of hardware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And that meant two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It meant you only had to write the program once, which was very important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And it meant that you could, in fact, if you were a random engineer, physicist, whatever,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: you could write that program yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: You didn't have to hire a programmer to do it for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: It might not be as good as you'd get with a real programmer, but it was pretty good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And so it democratized and made much more broadly available the ability to write code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: So it puts the power of programming into the hands of people like you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Anybody who wants to, who is willing to invest some time in learning a programming language

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: and is not then tied to a particular kind of computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And then in the seventies, you get system programming languages of which C is the survivor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And what does system programming languages mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: Programming languages that would take on the kinds of things that would necessary to write

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: so-called system programs, things like text editors or assemblers or compilers or operating

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: systems themselves, those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: And for-

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: That's to be feature rich.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: They have to be able to do a lot of stuff, a lot of memory management, the access processes

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: and all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: They have to-

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Kernighan: UNIX, C, AWK, AMPL, and Go Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #109

body.input: They have a lot of processing to-
