metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Yeah, so I guess,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: definitely have to check out the whole series

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: to really get his perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: but I'll do my best to condense it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Life itself, all forms of life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: they're dependent on energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Energy fuels everything, fuels life in action and motion

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: and all of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And we could say that maybe like a plant

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: is harnessing solar energy

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: and then reallocating that into growth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So its aim is to grow towards the sun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So it's allocating energy towards its goal

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: of harnessing more solar energy kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So, and humans too have evolved

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: to figure out how to harness energy in different ways

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: to satisfy higher and more complicated aims.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So the original energy network

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: that he referenced was fire, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: We actually learned to wield fire

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: as a tool in and of itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So not only are we learning to channel energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: but we actually learned how to isolate energy

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: as a tool in and of itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So we went into that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: how harnessing fire had changed human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And actually, this is one of the earliest examples too

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: of a co-evolution between tool and our biology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: because when we developed fire, we developed cooking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And cooking is, you can kind of think of it

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: as pre-digestion in a way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: We're liberating these macronutrients

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: or making things that otherwise would not be digestible,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: edible, and it increases the efficiency

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: by which we extract nutrients from food.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: That's what cooking does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So when we figured out cooking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: we liberated all these digestive resources

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: that were reallocated towards higher cognitive development.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So there's this evolutionary path

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: between figuring out fire and us becoming smarter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: which was interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Some other early examples he gave,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: he went into were missiles and hydraulics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So missiles being, we learned to hunt at a distance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: We can't bring down a wooly mammoth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: maybe with spears and up close and personal force,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: but we could with spears and javelins

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: and slings and whatnot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And then he went into how we've used water

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: to channel hydraulic energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So we can basically overcome gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: We can move, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: there's theories that the pyramids were constructed using,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: the blocks were moved using hydraulic energy

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: or using water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Clearly we use like cargo ships and whatnot

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: to move things much more efficiently across water

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: than we could the land.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So his whole view is how we keep figuring out better ways

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: and more efficient ways to harness energy and channel it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And in that perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: money has always represented a claim

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: on all other forms of energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So whatever energy couldn't be channeled

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: towards something useful in the economy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: historically would go into gold mining.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So gold became this residual, this economic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: this token of the excess energy created

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: by the market economy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And then you could take that token of energy

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: and use it to redeem for any other form of energy

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: or any other products of energy itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So it's, I guess it's my best approximation of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And it just really shattered my worldview again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: because I'd always thought about it as time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Like we spend time sacrificing to obtain money

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: that we then redeem for commencement sacrifices

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: from others, but I'd never considered it purely as energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And then it also ties back into gold

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: where there was an energy expenditure

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: necessary to obtain gold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So there's a proof of work associated with obtaining gold

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: that protected its market value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: All right, so you had to expend, again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: if market value of gold is 2000 an ounce,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: you had to expend 1900 an ounce mining.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So it kept producers honest in a way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So do you think something like proof of stake

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: that's more about reputation than,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: than actual exertion, like energy can work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: No, I think proof of stake is inherently centralizing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: It's like the old Matthew principle,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: from those who have to those who have more will be given

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: from those who have not, everything will be taken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: That's what proof of stake is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: You need proof of work to embody skin in the game

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: in the marketplace, such that contributions are commensurate

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: with consideration received.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: That's how systems work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: What's the idea why proof of work

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: might incentivize decentralization?

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Do you worry that as Bitcoin becomes more powerful,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: it may become again more centralized?

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Well, the decentralization of Bitcoin

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: is largely driven by the nodes actually,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: which aren't actually mining.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: They're just choosing which rule set to implement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And then the mining network

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: is actually enforcing that rule set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So I think the mining network is inherently decentralized

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: in that really anyone with access to cheap energy

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: can become a miner.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: You can freely enter or exit the market

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: or the network at any time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: But maintaining the block size at a manageable level

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: is what's key to maintaining node decentralization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: This is an interesting question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Who do you think has more power, the miners or the nodes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Because the nodes carry the idea of the protocol,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: like the specifics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So in some sense, they have more power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: If Bitcoin is an idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: But then-

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: They're kind of mutually indispensable though,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: because you can't have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: there's no security without the miners.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So without the miners, Bitcoin is just an idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And the idea of Bitcoin is maybe existed

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: even before Bitcoin, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Just sound money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: We just say sound money is an idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: But there was no way to root that

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: into thermodynamic reality without Satoshi figuring out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: not just proof of work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: it's the entire composite of the difficulty adjustment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: proof of work, one-way hashing, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So I don't know, that's hard to say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: hard to disentangle the two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: You've talked about money as morality too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: How do you think about moral and immoral action

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: in the context of money?

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And there's this great quote by Rothbard,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: who's a famous Austrian economist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And he says, quote, to be moral, an act must be free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Unquote.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And I think morality, it changes over time

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: and it has its roots in biology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Jordan Peterson makes the point that even animals

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: have their own sort of pseudo morality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: With wolf packs, for instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: if there's a dispute between the alpha males,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: or I guess between an alpha male and an incumbent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: the two males will have a fight basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And then when one is decided that one has won,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: the loser will basically roll over and give up his neck

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: to the alpha male.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And they do this instead of fighting to the death

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: because in a wolf pack, they need every wolf

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: so they can go out and bring down,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: you never know when you're gonna need the 20th wolf

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: to bring down the big buffalo the next day or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So they've developed this less than fight to the death

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: social morality to optimize their effectiveness

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: as a wolf pack.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And similarly for humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: our morality sort of emerges through competition

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: and play even.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: There are these implicit rules that come into place

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: based on how we're organizing ourselves over time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: With money, it's interesting because most tools

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: we would consider to be amoral,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: as in a hammer can be used to build a house,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: which could be seen to be good, like a good

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: constructive purpose or could be used to bash someone's skull,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: which could be something evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: And that the tool itself is amoral,

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: doesn't have any independent morality of its own.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: All of the morality is associated with the wielder

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: of the tool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: So what's the quote?

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: Like any tool can be a weapon if you hold it right

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: sort of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

metadata.title: Podcast: Robert Breedlove: Philosophy of Bitcoin from First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #176

body.input: when you monopolize money,

body.input: it's only useful as a tool for one thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: about your feelings. I was always uncomfortable with this. I mean, he's just being spiffy or

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: whatever, but I was always uncomfortable with somehow first that the hubris of thinking that

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: humans can arrive at absolute truth, which is what I assume he means by facts, like things that are

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: uncontrovertible, and then somehow deriding feelings, like feelings are not important. To me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: like, the whole thing is reality. Facts don't even, like, facts is reality, feelings are reality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: like the entirety of human experience is reality. All these consciousnesses somehow interacting

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: together, making up random crap and together agreeing that we're all going to wear the same

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: colors rooting for one football team or the other football team or countries, all those things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: that's real, because we've agreed that it's real. And in the same way, it gives us meaning. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: that same way religion is a set of ideas that gives us meaning. But, you know, real, it's really a

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: difficult for me as a scientist that finds comfort in the physical understanding of the universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: of physics, you know, I love physics, I love computer science. It makes me feel like everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: is perfectly understandable. And then I look at humans, they're totally not understandable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: It's like a giant mess, but that's part of the beauty. Like, what is love? Like, what the hell

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: is love? It's certainly not like a weird hack to convince me to procreate, because it feels

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: something bigger than that. So like, taking a purely evolutionary biologist perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: it's missing the, it's not missing, it's only capturing a part of the picture. And so it just

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: keeps making me ask, what is real? Because as a human, it's very human centric, it does certainly

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: feel like a part, a big part of what is real is all the fake stuff my mind makes up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: I mean, okay, I guess, is there something you could say from our discussions about the tools

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: of psychedelics, about our discussion about religion, of what is real, of what is reality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: These are largely unanswerable questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: But we do have to think about that. And I think that's a good point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: But we should nevertheless strive to answer them. That's the whole point of the human experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: And I think science is one way and religion is another. And I think there's actually a sphere

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: where they intersect, you know, there's a way for religion to be observable, testable, repeatable,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: falsifiable. When I look at the ancient mysteries, that that's what I find. I think I find people

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: exploring alternate states of consciousness and arriving at conclusions based on that exploration

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: and deriving deep meaning from that, which yes, are feelings and emotions and very hard to quantify.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: But nonetheless, these are the things that govern our lives. I mean, I don't know a parent who isn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: motivated by the love of their children. Everything I do at 40 years old now is pretty much inspired

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: by my love for my two daughters. And I can't prove to you that I love them. I can say it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: I can show you behavior, but it's very hard for me to weigh and measure that. So not everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: is so reducible to this quantifiable reality. And yet I also love science and I love the historical

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: process of weighing this data. I love the chemistry, I love the biology. And for me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: I think this was the message of the ancient Greeks. And I think this is the world in which

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: paleo-Christianity was born. I think there is this meeting ground between science and religion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: which allow for the, if not the discovery, then at least the near identification of the ultimate

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: reality, which is another way to describe God, right? This being a being is the transcendent

body.input: mystery. So speaking of God, you mentioned to me offline, you're wearing the most sophisticated

body.input: clothing choice of the elite intellectuals. Like you mentioned, Sam Harris was wearing a hoodie.

body.input: This is the Sam Harris hoodie. He's starting a trend. He's starting a trend.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: This is a new religion, you could even say. It's a ritual. It's a ritual practice

body.input: of intellectuals, of searching for meaning. So there's quite a fascinating debate. So he was

body.input: the role of religion in society and the role of science. And then on the other side, another

body.input: that I think will continue about the role of religion in society. For Jordan, there's all

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: these flaws with religion, but there is a lot of value to be discovered amidst the rituals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: And yet there it is. There's the data. And I don't see how you walk away from that. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: the purely physical plane will have resonances within that are those of our innermost being

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: and reality. You talked about the true reality, absolute truth. These are all constructs. And I

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: think they're constructs that are made day by day and acquire this aura of factuality. Remember in

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: Clifford Geertz's definition of religion, we're all just faking it until we make it. And I think a

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: lot of that has to do with moods and motivations and feelings and emotions, which is not to discredit

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: facts and figures. But I think that meaning, meaning making is a very subjective process

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: that is not only difficult to talk about, but difficult to quantify.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: And experience is a primary in that versus... So like the actual subjective experience is

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: primary to the meaning making process versus like some kind of rigorous analysis of like

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: having an algorithm that runs and computes and then finally spits out 42.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: Well, this is how families are created. Tell me more about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: Well, my wife and I fell in love and made babies. We didn't type up an Excel sheet

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: and figure out the best way to go about this. That's what I've been doing all these years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: That's why I'm single.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: Too many Excel sheets. Well, we say falling in love, right? We say fall in love. What does that

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: mean to fall in love? You are surrendering to an intelligence that is beyond us. You could say a

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: God-like intelligence. Richard Rohr, the Franciscan friar I mentioned, in the universal Christ,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: he writes a lot about how the divine for you is often encountered in the other. In fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: how could it be otherwise? This is bedrock sacramental theology that you find the God

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: in the things in your life as well you should. That's the proving ground for identifying as God

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: rather than creating relationship with God. And so I think that these irrational states play a big

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: role in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: Irrational. Well, I don't think there's a better way to end it than on the topic of love. Brian,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: thank you so much for a brilliant exposition of history and the poetry. I really appreciate you

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: talking with me today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: I love you, Lex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: I love you too, Brian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: Thanks for listening to this conversation with Brian Yorescu. And thank you to Inside Tracker,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: GiveWell, N.I., Indeed, and Masterclass. Check them out in the description to support this podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words from Terrence McKenna about psychedelics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: Part of what psychedelics do is they decondition you from cultural values. This is what makes it

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

body.input: such a political hot potato. Since all culture is a kind of con game, the most dangerous candy you

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Brian Muraresku: The Secret History of Psychedelics | Lex Fridman Podcast #211

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And likewise, there's no reason to think that the aftermath of our big

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: bang ends just at the boundary of what we can see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Indeed, there are quite strong arguments that it probably goes on about a hundred

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: times further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: It may even go on so much further that all combinatorials are replicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And there's another set of people like us sitting in a room like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: The following is a conversation with Lord Martin Rees, emeritus professor of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: cosmology and astrophysics at Cambridge University and co-founder of the Center

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: for the Study of Existential Risk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And now, dear friends, here's Martin Rees.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: In your 2020 Scientific American article, you write that, quote, today we know that

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the universe is far bigger and stranger than anyone suspected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So what do you think are the strangest, maybe the most beautiful or maybe even

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the most terrifying things lurking out there in the cosmos?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Well, of course, we're still groping for any detailed understanding of the remote

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: parts of the universe, but of course, what we've learned in the last few decades

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: is really two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: First, we've understood that the universe had an origin about 13.8 billion years ago

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: in a so-called Big Bang, a hot, dense state whose very beginnings are still shrouded

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: in mystery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And also we've learned more about the extreme things in it, black holes, neutron

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: stars, explosions of various kinds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And one of the most potentially exciting discoveries in the last 20 years, mainly

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the last 10, has been the realization that most of the stars in the sky are

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: orbited by retinues of planets, just as the sun is orbited by the Earth and the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: other familiar planets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And this, of course, makes the night sky farmer interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: What you see up there aren't just points of light, but there are planetary systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And that raises the question, could there be life out there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And so that is an exciting problem for the 21st century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So when you see all those lights out there, you immediately imagine all the planetary

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: worlds that are around them and they potentially have all kinds of different lives,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: living organisms, life forms or different histories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Well, that we don't know at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: We know that these planets are there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: We know that they have masses and orbits rather like the planets of our solar system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But we don't know at all if there's any life out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: We don't know at all if there's any life on any of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: I mean, it's entirely logically possible that life is unique to this Earth, doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: exist anywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: On the other hand, it could be that the origin of life is something which happens

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: routinely given conditions like the young Earth, in which case there could be

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: literally billions of places in our galaxy where some sort of biosphere has evolved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And settling where the truth lies between those two extremes is a challenge for the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So certainly we're either lucky to be here or very, very, very lucky to be here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: I guess that's the difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Where do you fall?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Your own estimate, your own guess on this question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Are we alone in the universe?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: I think we're foolish to give any firm estimate because we just don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And that's just an example of how we are depending on greater observations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And also, incidentally, in the case of life, we've got to take account of the fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that, as I always say to my scientific colleagues, biology is a much harder subject

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: than physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And most of the universe, if you know about it, could be understood by physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But we've got to remember that even the smallest living organism, an insect, is far

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: more complicated with layer on layer complexity than the most complicated star or galaxy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: You know, that's the funny thing about physics and biology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: The dream of physicists in the 20th century and maybe this century is to discover the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: theory of everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And there's a sense that once you discover that theory, you will understand everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: If we unlock the mysteries of how the universe works, would you be able to understand how

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: life emerges from that fabric of the universe that we understand?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: I think the phrase theory of everything is very misleading because it's used to describe

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: a theory which unifies the three laws of microphysics, electricity, magnetism, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: weak interaction with gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So it's an important step forward for particle physicists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But the lack of such a theory doesn't hold up any other scientists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Anyone doing biology or most of physics is not held up at all through not understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: subnuclear physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: They're held up because they're dealing with things that are very complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And that's especially true of anything biological.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So what's holding up biologists is not a lack of the so-called theory of everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: It's the inability to understand things which are very complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: What do you think we'll understand first, how the universe works or how the human body

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: works deeply, like from a fundamental deep level?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Well, I think perhaps we can come back to it later that there are only limited prospects

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of ever being able to understand with our human brains the most fundamental theories

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: linking together all the forces of nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: I think that may be a limitation of the human brains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But I also think that we can, perhaps aided by computer simulations, understand a bit

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: more of the complexity of nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But even understanding a simple organism from the atom up is very, very difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And I think extreme reductionists have a very misleading perception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: They tend to think that in a sense we are all solutions to Schrodinger's equation, etc.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But that isn't the way we'll ever understand anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: It may be true that we are reductives in the sense that we believe that that's the case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: We don't believe in any special life force in living things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But nonetheless, no one thinks that we can understand a living thing by solving

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Schrodinger's equation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: To take an example which isn't as complicated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: lots of people study the flow of fluids like water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Why waves break?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Why flows go turbulent?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: This is a serious branch of applied mathematics and engineering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And in doing this, you have concepts of viscosity, turbulence, and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Now, you can understand quite a lot about how water behaves and how waves break

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: in terms of those concepts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But the fact that any breaking wave is a solution of Schrodinger's equation for 10 to 30 particles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: even if you could solve that, which you clearly can't, would not give you any insight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So the important thing is that every science has its own irreducible concepts

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: in which you get the best explanation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So it may be in chemistry, things like valence, in biology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the concepts in cell biology, and in ecology, there are concepts like imprinting, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And in psychology, there are other concepts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So in a sense, the sciences are like a tall building where you have basic physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the most fundamental, then the rest of physics, then chemistry, then cell biology, et cetera,

body.input: And the limits, yes. Well, let me actually just

body.input: stroll around the beautiful and the strange of the universe. Over 20 years ago, you hypothesized that

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: First, what is dark matter and why has it been so tough to figure out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Well, I mean, we learned that galaxies and other large scale structures, which are moving around,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: but preventive flying apart by gravity, would be flying apart if they only contain the stuff we see,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: if everything in them was shining. And to understand how galaxies form,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and why they do remain confined to the same size, one has to infer that there's about five times

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: as much stuff producing gravitational forces than the total amount of stuff in the gas and stars

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that we see. And that stuff is called dark matter. That's like the leading name, it's not dark,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: it's just transparent, et cetera. And the most likely interpretation is that it's not dark,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: but the most likely interpretation is that it's a swarm of microscopic particles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: which have no electric charge and the very small cross-sections were hitting each other

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and hitting anything else. So they swarm around and we can detect their collective effects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And when we do computer simulations of how galaxies form and evolve and how they emerge

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: in the universe, we get a nice consistent picture if we put in five times as much mass in the form

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of these mysterious dark particles. And for instance, it works better if we think they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: not interacting particles than if we think they're a gas, which would have shock waves and things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So we know something about the properties of these, but we don't know what they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And the disappointment compared to my guess 20 years ago is that particles aren't

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: seeing this description and not yet been found. It was thought that the big accelerator,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the Large Hadrock Collider at CERN, which is the world's biggest, might have found a new

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: class of particles, which would have been the obvious candidates. And it hasn't. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: some people say, well, dark matter can't be there, et cetera. But what I would argue is that there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: a huge amount of parameter space that hasn't been explored. There are other kinds of particles

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: called axions, which behave slightly differently, which are good candidates. And there's a factor

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of 10 powers of 10 between the heaviest particles that could be created by the Large Hadrock Collider

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and the heaviest particles, which on theoretical grounds could exist without turning into black

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: holes. So there's a huge amount of possible particles which could be out there as remnants

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of the Big Bang, but which we wouldn't be able to detect so easily. So the fact that we've got new

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: constraints on what the dark matter could be doesn't diminish my belief that it's there in

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the form of particles because we've only explored a small fraction of parameter space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So there's this search. You're literally, upon an unintended, are searching in the dark here in this

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: giant parameter space of possible particles. You're searching for, I mean, there could be all kinds of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: particles. There could be, and there's some which may be very, very hard to detect. But I think we

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: can hope for some new theoretical ideas because one point which perhaps you'd like to discuss more is

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: about the very early stages of the Big Bang. And the situation now is that we have an outline picture

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: for how the universe has evolved from the time when it was expanding in just a nanosecond

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: up to the present. And we could do that because after nanosecond, the physics of the material

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: is in the same range that we can test in the lab. After a nanosecond, the particles move around like

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: those in the Large Hadron Collider. If you wait for one second, they're rather like in the centers

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of the hottest stars and nuclear reactions produce hydrogen, helium, et cetera, which fit the data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So we can, with confidence, extrapolate back to when the universe was a nanosecond old. Indeed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: I think we can do it with as much confidence as anything a geologist tells you about the early

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305
