body.input: history of the Earth. And that's huge progress in the last 50 years. But any progress puts in sharper

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: focus new mysteries. And of course, the new mysteries in this context are why is the universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: expanding the way it is? Why does it contain this mixture of atoms and dark matter and radiation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And why does it have the properties which allow a galaxy to form being fairly smooth, but not

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: completely smooth? And the answer to those questions are generally believed to lie in a

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: much, much earlier stage of the universe when conditions were much more extreme and therefore

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: far beyond the stage where we had the foothold in experiments, very theoretical. And so we don't have

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: a convincing theory. We just have ideas until we have something like string theory or some other

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: clues to the ultra-early universe. That's going to remain speculative. So there's a big gap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And to say how big the gap is, if we take the observable universe out to a bit more than 10

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: billion light years, then when the universe was a nanosecond old, that would have been squeezed

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: down to the size of our solar system or compressed into that volume. But the times we're talking

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: about when the key properties of the universe were first imprinted were times when that entire

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: universe was squeezed down to the size of a tennis ball or baseball, if you prefer, and to emerge from

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: something microscopic. So it's a huge extrapolation. And it's not surprising that since it's so far from

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: our experimental range of detectability, we are still groping for ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But you think first theory will reach into that place and then experiment will perhaps one day

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: catch up? Maybe simulation? Well, I think in a sense, it's a combination. I think what we hope for

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: is that there'll be a theory which applies to the early universe, but which also has consequences

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: which we can test in our present day universe, like discovering mind,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: nutrient does exist or things like that. And that's the thing which, as I mentioned,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: we may perhaps need a bit of AI to help us to calculate. But I think the hope would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that we will have a theory which applies under the very, very extreme early stages of the universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: but which gains credibility and gains confidence, because it also manages to account for otherwise

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: unexplained features of the low-energy world and what people call the standard model of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: particle physics, where there are lots of undetermined numbers. So it may help with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So we're dancing between physics and philosophy a little bit, but what do you think

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: happened before the Big Bang? So this seems, this feels like something that's out of the reach of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: science. It's out of the reach of present science, because science develops and as the front is

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: advanced, then new problems come into focus that couldn't even be postulated before. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: if I think of my own career, when I was a student, the evidence for the Big Bang was pretty weak,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: whereas now it's extremely strong. But we are now thinking about the reason why the universe is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: way it is and all that. So I would put all these things we've just mentioned in the category of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: speculative science. And I don't see a bifurcation between that and philosophy. But of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: to answer your question, if we do want to understand the very early universe, then we've

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: got to realize that it may involve even more counterintuitive concepts than quantum theory

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: does, because it's a condition even further away from everyday world than quantum theory is. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: remember our lives, our brains evolved and haven't changed much since our ancestors roamed the African

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: savanna and looked at the everyday world. And it's rather amazing that we've been able to make some

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: sense of the quantum micro world and of the cosmos. But there may be some things which are beyond us

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and certainly, as we implied, there are things that we don't yet understand at all. And of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: one concept we might have to jettison is the idea of three dimensions of space and time just ticking

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: away. There are lots of ideas. I mean, I think Stephen Hawking had an idea that talking about

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: what happened before the Big Bang, it's like asking what happens if you go north from the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: North Pole? It somehow closes off. That's just one idea. I don't like that idea, but that's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: possible one. And so we just don't know what happened at the very beginning of the Big Bang,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: whether many Big Bangs rather than one, etc. And those are issues which we may be able to get some

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: foothold on from some new theory. But even then, we won't be able to directly test the theories. But

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: I think it's a heresy to think you have to be able to test every prediction of a theory. Let me give

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: you another example. We take seriously what Einstein's theory says about the inside of black

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: holes, even though we can't observe them, because that theory has been vindicated in many other

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: places in cosmology and black holes, gravitational waves and all those things. Likewise, if we had a

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: theory which explains some things about the early history of our Big Bang and the present universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: then we would take seriously the inference if it predicted many Big Bangs, not one, even though we

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: can't predict the other ones. So the example is that we can take seriously a prediction if it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the consequence of a theory that we believe on other grounds. We don't need to be able to detect

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: another Big Bang in order to take it seriously. It may not be a proof, but it's a good indication

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that this is the direction where the truth lies. Yeah, if the theory is gained confidence in other

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: ways. Where do you sense? Do you think there's other universes besides our own? There are sort

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of well-defined theories which make assumptions about the physics at the relevant time. And this

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: time, incidentally, is 10 to the power minus 36 seconds or earlier than that. So this tiny sliver

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of time. And there are some theories, a famous one due to Andrei Linde, the Russian cosmologist

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: now at Stanford called eternal inflation, which did predict an eternal production of new Big Bangs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: as it were. And that's based on specific assumptions about the physics. But those assumptions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of course, are just hypotheses which aren't vindicated. But there are other theories which

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: only predict one Big Bang. So I think we should be open-minded and not dogmatic about these options

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: until we do understand the relevant physics. But there are these different scenarios of very

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: different ideas about this. But I think all of them have the feature that physical reality is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: lot more extensive than what we can see through our telescope. Even most conservative astronomers

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: would say that because we can see out with our telescopes to a sort of horizon, which is about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: depending on how you measure it, maybe 15 billion light years away or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But that horizon of observations is no more physical reality than the horizon around you

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: if you're in the ocean. And looking out at your horizon, there's no reason to think that the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: ocean ends just beyond your horizon. And likewise, there's no reason to think that the aftermath of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: our Big Bang ends just at the boundary of what we can see. Indeed, there are quite strong arguments

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that it probably goes on about 100 times further. It may even go on so much further that all

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: combinatorials are replicated. And there's another set of people like us sitting in a room like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Every possible combination of... Yeah, that could happen. That's not logically impossible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But I think many people would accept that it does go on and contain probably a million times as much

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: stuff as what we can see within a horizon. The reason for that, incidentally, is that if we look

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: as far as we can in one direction and in the opposite direction, then the conditions don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: differ by more than one part in 100,000. So that means that if we're part of some finite structure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the gradient across the part we can see is very small. And so that suggests that it probably does

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: go on a lot further. And the best estimates say it must go on at least 20 times further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Is that exciting or terrifying to you? Just the spans of it all, the wide, everything that lies

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: beyond the horizon, that example doesn't even hold for Earth. So it goes way, way farther.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And on top of that, just to take your metaphor further on the ocean, while we're on top of this

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: ocean, not only can we not see beyond the horizon, we also don't know much about the depth of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: ocean nor the actual mechanism of observation that's in our head. Yes. No, I think the rules

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and how to resolve those points you make. Yes. Yes. But I think even the solar system is pretty

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: vast by human standards. And so I don't think the perception of this utterly vast cosmos

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: need have any deeper impact on us than just realizing that we are very small on the scale

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of the external world. Yeah. It's humbling though. It's humbling and depending where your ego is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: it's humbling. Well, if you start off very unhumble indeed, it may make a difference,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: but most of us, I don't think it makes much difference. And well, there's a more general

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: question, of course, about whether the human race as such is something which is very special.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Or if on the other hand, it's just one of many such species elsewhere in the universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: or indeed existing at different times in our universe. To me, it feels almost obvious that

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the universe should be full of alien life, perhaps dead alien civilizations, but just

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the vastness of space. And it just feels wrong to think of Earth as somehow special. It sure as heck

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: doesn't look that special. The more we learn, the less special it seems. Well, I mean, I don't agree

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: with that as far as life is concerned, because remember that we don't understand how life began

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: here on Earth. Yes. We don't understand, although we know there will be an evolution of simple life

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: to complex life, we don't understand what caused the transition between complex chemistry and the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: first replicating metabolizing entity we call alive. Yes. That's a mystery. And serious physicists

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and chemists are now thinking about it, but we don't know. So we therefore can't say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: was it a rare fluke? Yeah. Which would not have happened anywhere else. Or was it something

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: which involves a process that would have happened in any other planet where conditions were like

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: they were on the young Earth? So we can't say that now. I think many of us would indeed bet

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that probably some kind of life exists elsewhere. But even if you accept that, then there are many

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: contingencies going from simple life to present day life. And some biologists like Stephen J. Gould

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: thought that if you rerun evolution, you'd end up with something quite different, and maybe not

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: with an intelligent species. So the contingencies in evolution may militate against the emergence of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: intelligence, even if life gets started in lots of places. So I think these are still completely

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: open questions. And that's why it's such an exciting time now that we are starting to be able

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: to address these. I mean, I mentioned the fact that the origin of life is a question that we may

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: be able to understand and serious people are working on. It's usually put in the sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: too difficult box. Everyone knew it was important, but they didn't know how to tackle it or what

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: experiments to do. But it's not like that now. And that's partly because of cleverer experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But I think most importantly, because we are aware that we can look for life in other places,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: other places in our solar system, and of course, on the exoplanets around other stars. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: within 10 or 20 years, I think two things could happen, which will be really, really important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: We might, with the next big telescope, be able to image some of the Earth-like planets around

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: other stars. Image, like get a picture? Well, actually, let me caveat that it takes 50 years

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: to get a resolved image, but to actually detect the light. Because now, of course, these exoplanets

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: are detected by their effect on the parent star. They either cause their parent star to dim slightly

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: when they transit across in front of it. And so we see the dips or their gravitational pull

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: makes the star wobble a bit. So most of the 5,000 plus planets that have been found around other

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: stars, they've been found indirectly by their effect in one of those two ways on the parent star.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: You can still do a pretty good job of estimating size, all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: The size and the mass, you can estimate. But detecting the actual light from one of these

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: exoplanets hasn't really been done yet, except one or two very bright big planets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So maybe like James Webb Telescope would be. Well, James Webb may do this, but even better

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: will be the European ground-based telescope called Unimaginatively Extremely Large Telescope,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: which has a 39 meter diameter mirror, 39 meters, an isometric weight on sheets of glass.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And that will collect enough light from one of these exoplanets around a nearby star to be able

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: to separate out its light from that of the star, which is millions of times brighter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and get the spectrum of the planet and see if it's got oxygen or chlorophyll and things in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So that will come. James Webb may make some steps there. But I think we can look forward to learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: quite a bit in the next 20 years, because I like to say, supposing that aliens are looking at the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: solar system, then they see the sun as an ordinary star. They see the Earth as in Carl Sager's nice

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: phrase, a pale blue dot lying very close in the sky to its star. And then they see the sun as an

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: ordinary sky to its star, our sun, and much, much, much fainter. But if they could observe that dot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: they could learn quite a bit. They could perhaps get the spectrum of the light and find the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: atmosphere. They'd find the shade of blue is slightly different depending on whether the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Pacific Ocean or the land mass of Asia was facing them. So they could infer the length of the day

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and the ocean and continents, and maybe something about the seasons and the climate. And that's the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: kind of calculation and inference we might be able to draw within the next 10 or 20 years about other

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: exoplanets. And evidence of some sort of biosphere on one of them would, of course, be crucial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And it would rule out the still logical possibilities that life is unique. But there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: another way in which this may happen in the next 20 years. People think there could be something

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: swimming under the ice of Europa and Enceladus, and probes are being sent to maybe not quite go

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: under the ice, but detect the spray coming out to see if there's evidence for organics in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And if we found any evidence for an origin of life that happened in either of those places,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that would immediately be important. Because if life has originated twice independently in one

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: planetary system, the solar system, that would tell us straight away it wasn't a rare accident,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and must have happened billions of times in the galaxy. At the moment, we can't rule out it being

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: unique. And incidentally, if we found life on Mars, then that would still be ambiguous, because

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: people have realized that this early life could have got from Mars to Earth or vice versa on

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: meteorites. So if you found life on Mars, then some skeptics could still say if it's a single

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: origin. But I think... But Europa is far enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: That's far enough away, yeah. Statistically because...

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So that's why that would be especially... It's always the skeptics that ruin a good party.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But we need them, of course. We need them at the party. We need some skeptics at the party.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But boy, would that be so exciting to find life on one of the moons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Yeah. Because it means that life is everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: That'll just be any kind of vegetation or life. The question of the aliens or science fiction

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: is a different matter. Intelligent aliens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Yeah. But if you have a good indication that there's life elsewhere in the solar system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that means life is everywhere. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And that... Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: I don't know if that's terrifying or what that is, because if life is everywhere,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: why is intelligent life not everywhere? Why... I mean, you've talked about that most likely

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: alien civilizations, if they are out there, they would likely be far ahead of us, the ones that

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: would actually communicate with us. Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And that... Again, one of those things that is both exciting and terrifying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: You've mentioned that they're likely not to be of biological nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Well, I think that's important. Of course, again, it's a speculation, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: in speculating about intelligent life. And I take the search seriously. In fact, I chair the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: committee that the Russian-American investor Yuri Milner supports looking for intelligent life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: He's putting $10 million a year into better equipment and getting time on telescopes to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: this. And so I think it's worthwhile, even though I don't hold my breath for success, it's very

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: exciting. But that does lead me to wonder what might be detected. And I think, well, we don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: know, we've got to be open minded about anything, we've no idea what it will be. And so any

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: anomalous objects, or even some strange shiny object in the solar system or anything we've got

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: to keep our eyes open for. But I think if we ask what about a planet like the Earth where evolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: had taken more of the same track, then as you say, it wouldn't be synchronized. If it had lagged

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: behind, then of course, it would not have got to advanced life, but it may have had a head start.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: It may have formed on a planet around an older star. But then let's ask what we would see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: It's taken nearly 4 billion years from the first life to us. And we've now got this technological

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: civilization, which could make itself detectable to any alien life, aliens out there. But I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: most people would say that this civilization of flesh and blood creatures in a collective civilization

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: may not last more than a few hundred years more. I think that some people would say it will kill

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: itself off. But I'm more optimistic. And I would say that what we're going to have in future is

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: no longer the slow Darwinian selection, but we're going to have what I call secular intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: design, which will be humans designing their progeny to be better adapted to where they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And if they go to Mars or somewhere, they're badly adapted and they want to adapt a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And so they will adapt. But there may be some limits to what could be done with flesh and blood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And so they may become largely electronic, download their brains and be electronic entities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And if they're electronic, then what's important is that they're near immortal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And also they won't necessarily want to be on a planet with an atmosphere or gravity. They may

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: go off into the blue yonder. And if they're near immortal, they won't be daunted by interstellar

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: travel taking a long time. And so if we looked at what would happen on the Earth in the next

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: millions of years, then there may be these electronic entities which have been sent out

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and are now far away from the Earth, but still sort of burping away in some fashion to be detected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And so this therefore leads me to think that if there was another planet which had evolved

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: like the Earth and was ahead of us, it wouldn't be synchronized. So we wouldn't see a flesh and

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: blood civilization, but we would see these electronic progeny as it were. And then this

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: raises another question because there's the famous argument against there being lots of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: aliens out there, which is that they would come and invade us and eat us or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: That's a common idea, which is fair to me as attributed to have been the first to say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And I think there's an escape clause to that because these entities would be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: they evolved by second intelligence design, designed by their predecessors and then designed by us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Whereas Darwinian selection requires two things, it requires aggression and intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: This future in tele design may favor intelligence because that's what they were designed for,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: but it may not favor aggression. And so these future entities, they may be sitting deep thoughts,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: they may be sitting deep thoughts, thinking deep thoughts and not being at all expansionist. So

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: they could be out there. And we can't refute their existence in the way the Fermi paradox is

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: supposed to refute their existence because these would not be aggressive or expansionist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Well, maybe evolution requires competition, not aggression. And I wonder if competition can take

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: forms that are non-expansionary so you can still have fun competing in the space of ideas,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: which may be primarily- They'd all be philosophers perhaps, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: In a way, right. It's an intellectual exercise versus a sort of violent exercise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So what does this civilization on Mars look like? So do you think we would more and more

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: maybe start with some genetic modification and then move to basically cyborgs, increasing

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: integration of electronic systems, computational systems into our bodies and brains?

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: This is a theme of my other new book out this year, which is called The End of Astronauts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: The End of Astronauts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Co-written with my old friend and colleague from Berkeley, Don Goldsmith. And it's really about

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the role of human spaceflight versus sort of robotic spaceflight. And just to summarize

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: what it says, it argues that the practical case for sending humans into space is getting weaker

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: all the time as robots get better and more capable. Robots 50 years ago couldn't do anything very

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: much, but now they could assemble big structures on space or in space or on the moon. And they can

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and they could probably do exploration. Well, present ones on Mars can't actually do the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: geology, but future AI will be able to do the geology and already they can dig on Mars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And so if you want to do exploration of Mars and of course, even more of Enceladus or Europa,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: where you could never send humans, we depend on robots. And they're far, far cheaper because

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: to send a human to Mars requires feeding them for 200 days on the journey there and bringing

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: them back and neither of those are necessary for robots. So the practical case for humans is

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: getting very, very weak. And if humans go, it's only as an adventure really. And so the line in

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: our book is that human spaceflight should not be pursued by NASA or public funding agencies

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: because it has no practical purpose, but also because it's especially expensive if they do it

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: because they would have to be risk averse in launching civilians into space. I can illustrate

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that by noting that the shuttle was launched 135 times and it had two spectacular failures,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: which each killed the seven people in the crew. And it had been mistakenly presented as safe

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: for civilians. And there was a woman school teacher killed in one of them. It was a big

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: national trauma and they tried to make it safer still. But if you launch into space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: just the kind of people prepared to accept that sort of risk and of course, test pilots and

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: people who go hang gliding and go to the South Pole, et cetera, are prepared to accept a 2% risk

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: at least for a big challenge. Then of course you do it more cheaply. And that's why I think human

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: spaceflight should be left to the billionaires and their sponsors because then the taxpayers aren't

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: paying and they can launch simply those people who are prepared to accept high risks, space

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: adventure, not space tourism. And we should cheer them on. And as regards where they would go,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: then low Earth orbit, I suspect, can be done quite cheaply in future. But going to Mars,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: which is very, very expensive and dangerous for humans, the only people who would go would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: these adventurers maybe on one-way trip like some of the early polar explorers and Magellan

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and people like that. And we would cheer them on. And I expect and I've ever hoped that by the end

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of the century, there will be a small community of such people on Mars who will be able to go

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: to Mars. Living very uncomfortably, far less comfortably than at the South Pole or the bottom

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: of the ocean or the top of Everest. But they will be there and they won't have a certain ticket,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: but they'll be there. Incidentally, I think it's a dangerous illusion to think as Elon Musk

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: has said that we can have mass emigration from the Earth to Mars to escape the Earth's problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: It's a dangerous illusion because it's far easier to deal with climate change on Earth

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: than to terraform Mars to make it properly habitable to humans. So there's no planet

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: B for ordinary risk averse people. But for these crazy adventurers, then you can imagine that they

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: would be trying to live on Mars as great pioneers. And by the end of the century, then there will be

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: huge advances compared to the present in two things. First, in understanding genetics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: So is the genetically redesigned one's offspring. And secondly, to use cyborg techniques to implant

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: something in our brain or indeed think about downloading, etc. And those techniques will,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: one hopes, be heavily regulated on Earth on prudentials and ethical grounds. And of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: we are pretty well adapted to the Earth. So we don't have the incentive to do these things in

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the way they were there. So our argument is that it'll be those crazy pioneers on Mars

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: using all these scientific advances, which will be controlled here, away from the regulators,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: they will transition into a new post human species. And so if they do that, and if they

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: transition into something which is electronic, eventually, because there may be some limits to

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the capacity of flesh and blood brains anyways, then those electronic entities may not want to

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: stay on the planet like Mars, they may want to go away. And so they'll be the precursors of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: future evolution of life and intelligence coming from the Earth. And of course, there's one point

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: which perhaps astronomers are more aware of than most people. Most people are aware that we are the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: outcome of 4 billion years of evolution. Most of them nonetheless, probably think that we humans

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: are somehow the culmination, the top of the tree. But no astronomers can believe that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: because astronomers know that the Earth is four and a half billion years old.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: The sun has been shining for that length of time, but the sun has got six billion years more to go

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: before it flares up and engulfs the inner planet. So the sun is less than halfway through its life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and the expanding universe goes on far longer still, maybe forever. And I'd like to quote Woody Allen,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: who said, eternity is very long, especially towards the end. So we shouldn't be so

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: so we shouldn't think of ourselves as maybe even the halfway stage in the emergence of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: cosmic complexity. And so these entities who are post-cursors, they will go beyond the solar system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And of course, even if there's nothing else out there already, then they could

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: populate the rest of the galaxy. And maybe eventually meet the others who are out there

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: expanding as well. Yeah, expanding, populating, with expanded capacity for life and intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: all those kinds of things. Well, they might. But again, all better off, because I can't conceive

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: what they'd be like. They won't be green men and women with eyes on stalks, you know, maybe something

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: quite different. We just don't know. But there is an interesting question, actually, which comes up

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: when I've sometimes spoken to audiences about this topic, that the question of consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and self-awareness, because you're going back to philosophical questions, I mean, whether an

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: electronic robot would be a zombie, or would it be conscious and self-aware? And I think there's no

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: way of answering this empirically. And some people think that consciousness and self-awareness is an

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: emergent property in any sufficiently complicated network that they would be. Others say, well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: maybe it's something special to the flesh and blood that we're made of. We don't know. And in a sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: this may not matter to the way things behave, because they could be zombies and still

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: behave as though they were intelligent. But I remember after one of my talks, someone came up

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and said, wouldn't it be sad if these future entities, which were the main intelligent

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: universe, had no self-awareness? So there was nothing which could appreciate the wonder and

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: mystery of the universe and the beauty of the universe in the way that we do. And so it does

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: perhaps affect one's perspective of whether you welcome or deplore this possible future scenario,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: depending on whether you think the future post-human entities are conscious and have

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: an aesthetic sense, or whether they're just zombies. And of course, you have to be humble

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: to realize that self-awareness may not be the highest form of being. That humans have a very

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: strong ego and a very strong sense of identity, like personal identity connected to this particular

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: brain. It's not so obvious to me that that is somehow the highest achievement of a life form

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that maybe this kind of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Think something collective would be...

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: It's possible that... Well, I think from an alien perspective, when you look at Earth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: it's not so obvious to me that individual humans are the atoms of intelligence. It could be the

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: entire organism together, the collective intelligence. And so we humans think of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: ourselves as individuals. We dress up, we wear ties and suits, and we give each other prizes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: But in reality, the intelligence, the things we create that are beautiful emerges from our

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: interaction with each other. And that may be where the intelligence is, ideas jumping from

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: one person to another over generations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Yes. But we have experiences where we can appreciate beauty and wonder and all that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And a zombie may not have those experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Yeah. Or it may have a very different... We have a very black and white harsh description of Zod,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: like a philosophical zombie. That could be just a very different way to experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And in terms of the explorers that colonize Mars,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: there's several things I want to mention. One, it's just at a high level. To me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: that's one of the most inspiring things humans can do, is reach out into the unknown. That's in

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: the space of ideas, in the space of science, but also the explorers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Yes. No, I agree with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: And that inspires people here on Earth more. I mean, it did when going to the moon or going

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: out to space in the 20th century, that inspired a generation of scientists. I think that also

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: could be used to inspire a generation of new scientists in the 21st century by reaching out

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: towards Mars. So in that sense, I think what Elon Musk and others are doing is actually quite

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: inspiring. It's not a recreational thing. It actually has a deep humanitarian purpose of

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: really inspiring the world. And then on the other one, to push back on your thought,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: I don't think Elon says, we want to escape Earth's problems. It's more that we should allocate some

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: small percentage of resources to have a backup plan. Because you yourself have spoken about and

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: written about all the ways we clever humans can destroy ourselves. And I'm not sure, it does seem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: when you look at the long arc of human history, it seems almost obvious that we need to become

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: a multi-planetary species over a period if we are to survive many centuries. It seems that

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: as we get clever and clever with the ways we can destroy ourselves, Earth is going to become less

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and less safe. So in that sense, this is one of the things, people talk about climate change,

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: and then we need to respond to climate change. And that's a long-term and very important thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: We need to respond to climate change and that's a long-term investment we need to make. But it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: not really long-term, it's a span of decades. I think what Elon is doing is a really long-term

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: investment. We should be working on multi-planetary colonization now if we were to have it ready five

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: centuries from now. And so taking those early steps. And then also there's something happens

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: when you go into the unknown and do this really difficult thing, you discover something very new.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: You discover something about robotics or materials engineering or nutrition or neuroscience or human

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: relations or political systems that actually work well with human history. You discover all those

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: things. And so it's a worthy effort to go out there and try to become cyborgs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: Yeah, no, I agree with that. I think the only different point I'd make is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: this is going to be very expensive if it's done in a risk averse way. And that's why I think we

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: should be grateful to the billionaires if they're going to foster these opportunities for

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305

body.input: thrill-seeking risk-takers who we can all admire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Martin Rees: Black Holes, Alien Life, Dark Matter, and the Big Bang | Lex Fridman Podcast #305
